title: Self-paced silent speech brain-computer interface for device control
abstractText: Abstract Brain-computer interfaces can potentially restore autonomy to people with paralysis, including the ability to control their own environment via smart devices in the home. BCI applications for controlling smart devices to date have required visual displays or auditory cues, limiting the user’s ability to autonomously and privately issue commands. In this study, a clinical trial participant with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) used a chronically implanted electrocorticographic (ECoG) BCI to control smart devices with self-paced silent speech commands. Across 18 experimental sessions, silently mimed speech commands were detected in real time and decoded with a median accuracy of 97.1% (chance: 7.14%) and the median correct decodes per minute was 11.86. These results demonstrate that silently attempted speech can be reliably decoded without exogenous timing cues, supporting the feasibility of reliable autonomous smart device control with an implantable BCI.

title: Protocol for constructing correlation-based molecular networks from large-scale untargeted metabolomics data
abstractText: This protocol describes a computational approach for constructing correlation-based molecular networks from untargeted metabolomics data using MetVAE, a variational autoencoder-based framework. Complementing spectral similarity networks, it captures functional relationships reflected in cross-sample correlations. The workflow imports metabolomics features and sample metadata, adjusts for compositionality, missingness, confounding, and high-dimensionality, estimates sparse metabolite correlations, and exports GraphML files for network visualization. In a hepatocellular carcinoma mouse model, it links lipid classes in high-fat-diet animals, suggesting an endogenous "auto-brewery" route to lipotoxic metabolites.

title: Vertical mesh-mediated fascial traction is associated with higher fascial closure rates than vacuum-assisted wound closure with mesh-mediated traction in open abdomen therapy
abstractText: Abstract Open abdomen treatment (OAT) is a critical surgical strategy for managing severe intra-abdominal conditions. Early definitive fascial closure (DFC) reduces complications and mortality. While the vacuum-assisted wound closure with mesh-mediated fascial traction (VAWCM) technique is considered the current standard, novel methods such as vertical mesh-mediated fascial traction (VMMFT) with devices like Fasciotens® Abdomen offer a promising alternative. This retrospective, registry-based, propensity score–matched cohort study compared fascial closure outcomes between VAWCM and VMMFT in patients undergoing OAT, utilizing data from the European Hernia Society Open Abdomen Registry (2015–2024). Patients were matched based on sepsis at OAT initiation and initial fascial defect width. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Chi-square and Mann–Whitney U tests, and logistic regression. Of 1119 OAT cases, 39 (3.5%) received VMMFT and 675 (60.3%) VAWCM. After matching, each cohort included 28 patients. In the matched cohorts, higher DFC rates were observed with VMMFT than with VAWCM in both the ITT-like (89.3% vs. 60.7%; p = .01) and PP-like analyses (100.0% vs. 69.6%; p = .01). Logistic regression in the matched cohort showed an association between VMMFT and higher odds of fascial closure (OR 5.39, 95% CI 1.31–22.25; p = .02), although the confidence interval was wide. ICU stay and ventilation duration were longer in the VMMFT group, while enteroatmospheric fistula occurred in 0% versus 10.7% of patients, respectively (p = .08). In this retrospective registry-based analysis, VMMFT was associated with higher fascial closure rates compared with VAWCM. Given the limited number of VMMFT cases, wide confidence intervals, and residual imbalance after propensity-score matching, these findings should be interpreted as observational, exploratory, and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Larger prospective studies using standardized treatment protocols are required to confirm this association. title: Nanocellulose-clay composites as substrates for printed humidity sensors
abstractText: Flexible and biodegradable nanocomposite films were developed as substrates of printed humidity sensors, using cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) that were reinforced with naturally abundant nanoclays, microfibrous sepiolite and lamellar cloisite. The addition of nanoclays to the CNF matrix led to notable changes in film morphology, surface roughness, wettability, and optical properties, as confirmed by structural, spectroscopic, and microscopic characterization. These modifications also improved the mechanical properties of the films, increasing stiffness and tensile strength. Importantly, bending tests revealed that the substrates preserved their mechanical and electrical functionality under repeated deformation, confirming their suitability for flexible electronic systems. The humidity sensing performance was evaluated by measuring impedance magnitude and phase responses across a range of relative humidity levels. The type and concentration of clay strongly influenced the sensing behavior; sepiolite enhanced water affinity and extended the detection range, while cloisite promoted a more capacitive response with greater phase sensitivity. Both nanocomposites demonstrated reliable signal stability and response linearity with sensitivities of –0.043 Ω/%RH and –0.071 Ω/%RH for sepiolite and cloisite nanocomposites, respectively, across wide relative humidity ranges. Additionally, the biodegradability of the sensors was proved in fungal growth assays. Overall, this study demonstrates that CNF-based nanocomposites containing natural clays offer a sustainable and tunable platform for the fabrication of flexible, low-impact humidity sensors and contribute to the advancement of transient and eco-friendly electronic technologies.

title: Dihydroberberine protects against diabetic nephropathy via inhibiting NF-B mediated inflammation and fibrosis
abstractText: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a serious complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by inflammation and fibrosis. Berberine has a favorable therapeutic effect in alleviating DN; however, its extremely low bioavailability limits its clinical use. Dihydroberberine (DHB) is a metabolite of berberine that has higher bioavailability, but its effect in alleviating DN remains unclear. DHB intervention alleviated hyperglycemia, renal dysfunction, and inflammation, while reducing pathological renal damage and fibrosis‑related gene expression in diabetic db/db and high-fat diet (HFD)-induced mice. Next, we investigated the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of DHB in alleviating DN using a combination of network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation. A public database was used to predict the 3706 targets involved in DN and the 456 targets of DHB. Promoter analysis of DN targets using HOMER motif analysis and Venn analysis revealed nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) as the only transcription factor in both groups, suggesting that it could be the main target of DHB in alleviating DN. Molecular docking confirmed the interaction between DHB and NF-κB. In vitro studies revealed that DHB improved the viability of high glucose–/palmitic acid–induced HK-2 cells; reduced NF-κB/p65 and cleaved caspase-3 levels; and suppressed inflammation, fibrosis, and apoptosis markers. In diabetic db/db and HFD-induced mice, DHB treatment also alleviated NF-κB–related inflammation and fibrosis-related gene expression. These findings suggest that DHB ameliorates DN via modulation of the NF-κB pathway, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate.

High-pressure impregnation and thermal stabilization of pine bark for reuse-oriented textile effluent polishing
abstractText: Dyes are widely used in the textile industry, and untreated dye-containing effluents pose major environmental risks. This study investigates pine bark (Pinus pinaster), a timber by-product, as a low-cost biosorbent for dye removal. Powdered and granular bark was impregnated with 10% (w/w) iron using Incipient Wetness Impregnation with sonication or High-Pressure Impregnation (HPI) at 75–300 MPa, followed by thermal treatment at 400 °C under nitrogen and hydrogen. Adsorption tests with a synthetic dye mixture (80 mg/L) showed that HPI at 150 MPa provided the best performance, achieving over 90% color removal with no iron leaching. Thermal treatment enhanced iron fixation and adsorption, producing the most effective material (G1FeTT). With real textile effluent, G1FeTT (5.0 g/L) achieved 83.5% dye removal with equilibrium at 16 h (2.12 mg/g). The Elovich model best described the kinetics. Treated effluent reuse in dyeing baths was feasible, enabling 25–75% freshwater substitution while maintaining acceptable color metrics.

Multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to extended Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstractText: Despite their profound consequences for the global carbon cycle, multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate long-term oceanic responses to atmospheric CO 2 forcing using the Model for Interdisciplinary Research on Climate, Earth System version 2 for Long-term simulations (MIROC-ES2L) Earth system model driven by extended Shared Socio-economic Pathway (SSP) scenarios through to the year 2500. Ocean–atmosphere p CO 2 disequilibrium exhibits strong scenario dependence. Under the low-emission scenario SSP1–2.6, oceanic CO 2 undersaturation gradually weakens and approaches near equilibrium by 2100. By contrast, under the high-emission scenario SSP5–8.5, rapid increase in atmospheric p CO 2 results in increasing undersaturation of CO 2 in the ocean over the 21st century. Thereafter, surface-ocean CO 2 supersaturation progressively expand into the equatorial and subtropical oceans between the mid–23rd and late 25th century. The Southern Ocean remains persistently undersaturated throughout the simulations, consistent with sustained influence from deep waters that are weakly affected by anthropogenic perturbations. Under SSP5–8.5, oceanic CO 2 uptake continues to increase until the late 21st century. Thereafter, it gradually weakens as surface-ocean p CO 2 approaches atmospheric levels, whereas the Southern Ocean remains a persistent carbon sink throughout the simulation. Across all scenarios, early oceanic p CO 2 changes are primarily driven by increases in dissolved inorganic carbon, whereas alkalinity becomes an increasingly important control from the mid–22nd century onward under SSP5–8.5. A progressive decline in the oceanic CO 2 buffering capacity, driven by cumulative CO 2 uptake, increases the sensitivity of surface-ocean p CO 2 to additional carbon uptake. The buffering capacity approaches its effective minimum levels by the late 22nd century. In parallel, enhanced upper-ocean stratification and a slowdown of the deep overturning circulation reduce the upward transport of high alkalinity waters to the surface. This results in a decline in surface-ocean alkalinity that further enhances the influence of alkalinity on surface-ocean p CO 2 during this period. Marine biological productivity and export vary significantly as a function of atmospheric CO 2 trajectory. It increases under low-emission scenarios but declines under sustained high-emission scenarios. The transition between the two behaviors occurs when pCO2atm reaches approximately 3 times the preindustrial level and is closely associated with the weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and the resulting nutrient redistribution. Thermal stress and nutrient limitation persist in regions such as the Arctic Ocean until the late 25th century even under SSP1–2.6, indicating a centennial-scale lagged response of marine ecosystems to atmospheric CO 2 forcing. In the surface ocean, marine ecosystem stress (integrating thermal and biogeochemical stressors) continues to intensify through the late 22nd century under SSP5–8.5, despite the stabilization of atmospheric p CO 2 , highlighting the long memory and limited reversibility of oceanic ecosystem stress.

title: A human-specific TAF8 isoform diversifies the composition of the TFIID general transcription factor
abstractText: Abstract Despite its central role in RNA polymerase II transcription, the composition and function of the TFIID general transcription factor can vary across tissues and developmental stages. Such variability may provide a substrate for evolutionary innovation and contribute to human-specific regulatory functions. Here, we identify a human-specific short isoform of TAF8 (TAF8s), a scaffold subunit of TFIID, generated through the use of an intronic polyadenylation site (iPAS). Comparative genomic analyses reveal that the genomic substrate for this isoform originated with the insertion of a FLAM-C Alu element into intron 5 in the common ancestor of anthropoid primates (Simiiformes), whereas subsequent small sequence changes at the Alu-associated iPAS coincide with the emergence of TAF8s expression in the human lineage. TAF8s lacks nearly half of the canonical TAF8 coding sequence, is widely expressed across human tissues, and accounts for a substantial fraction of TAF8 transcripts. It encodes a truncated protein lacking the canonical nuclear-localization signal and localizes predominantly to the cytoplasm. Despite retaining interactions with its histone-fold partner TAF10 and other core TFIID subunits, TAF8s loses interaction with TAF2, providing a molecular basis for alternative TFIID sub-complex formation. Together, our findings identify a recently evolved human-specific regulatory innovation at the TAF8 locus that diversifies the composition of a conserved general transcription factor. This example illustrates how evolution of transcript isoforms can generate new protein interactions and molecular complexity in essential cellular machineries, with potential implications for the functional diversification of TAF-containing complexes and the genetic basis of TAF-related developmental disorders.

title: Electronic Dynamics in Long Linear and Cyclic Polyynes
abstractText: Abstract Carbyne─the one-dimensional sp-hybridized allotrope of carbon─has long been predicted to exhibit unique properties, yet its synthesis remains elusive. To probe its behavior, finite sp-carbon chains such as cumulenes and polyynes have been studied. While much has been established about the ground-state properties of cumulenes and polyynes, our understanding of their photophysical dynamics, which gives critical insight into how electronic relaxation, structural reorganization, and spin formation evolve, has focused almost exclusively on short, linear systems, with little consideration of topology. Here, we investigate long 48-carbon linear and cyclic polyynes in the liquid phase using steady-state and ultrafast, temperature- and polarization-resolved optical and vibrational spectroscopy. We find highly delocalized ground states in both topologies, with softened Peierls distortion and reduced bond-length alternation relative to shorter chains. In contrast, the excited state singlet dipole depolarization mechanism and subsequent intersystem crossing are strongly dependent on chain length and topology. As in shorter polyynes, transient infrared spectroscopy shows that photoexcitation of long linear polyynes induces a cumulene-like excited-state geometry; however, this structural rearrangement is weaker and shorter-lived than in shorter analogues. Comparison with shorter-chain trends and theoretical predictions shows that the Huang–Rhys factor remains far below the ideal infinite-chain value at 48 carbons, suggesting that vibronic coupling grows more slowly at long chain length than expected from simple extrapolation. Our results reveal how topology influences the largely backbone-dominated electronic dynamics of long polyynes and refine our understanding of finite sp-carbon systems at longer chain lengths than previously accessible with such time-resolved methods.

Compact Wafer-Bonded Fabry–Perot Cavity-Based Photothermal Spectroscopy for Gas Sensing
abstractText: Abstract Currently available electrochemical and direct absorption gas sensor approaches suffer from weak molecular selectivity, challenges in miniaturization, and constraints in cost-effective large-scale manufacturing. In contrast, the integration of an interferometric cavity-assisted technique with photothermal spectroscopy (PTS) provides an alternative solution promising improved sensitivity and increased dynamic range. Here, we report a compact wafer-bonded Fabry–Perot (WB-FP) cavity fabricated using a Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) and demonstrate its use as a photothermal transducer for gas sensing. Unlike conventional manually assembled Fabry–Perot (FP) cavities, the proposed design defines cavity permenant alignment during fabrication, providing a pathway toward scalable and reproducible photonic gas sensors. In this architecture, a near-infrared (NIR) beam is collimated and propagated through a 500 μm spaced FP cavity to probe the photothermal effects induced by interactions between the target gas molecules and the optical pump beam inside the cavity volume. To demonstrate the applicability of the developed sensor system, the metrological figures of merit were evaluated using methane (CH4) as the targeted analyte across a range of concentrations. Targeting the absorption band centered at 6047 cm–1, the system achieves a minimum detection limit (MDL) of 42 ppm with a 1 s integration time. Allan deviation analysis further indicates an improved MDL of 5.1 ppm at an optimal integration time of 100 s, corresponding to a normalized noise-equivalent absorption (NNEA) coefficient of 3.27 × 10–7 cm–1 W Hz–1/2. These results highlight the potential of the wafer-bonded FP cavity as a scalable, compact transducer for photothermal gas sensing, bridging the route toward miniaturized, stable, cost-effective, and high-sensitivity gas technologies.

title: Learning Koopman Operators for Coupled Systems via Information on Governing Equations of Subsystems
abstractText: Nonlinear coupled systems are ubiquitous in science and engineering. The analysis and modeling of such systems are challenging due to their high dimensionality and complex interactions among subsystems. In recent years, operator-theoretic methods based on the Koopman operator have attracted attention as a powerful tool for analyzing and modeling nonlinear dynamical systems. Extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) is one of the most popular methods for approximating the Koopman operator. However, EDMD is a purely data-driven method, and it may be unstable and inaccurate for coupled systems under limited data availability. In this paper, we propose a method to construct a finite-dimensional Koopman matrix for coupled systems using the differential equations governing each subsystem. By regularizing the Koopman matrix toward a prior constructed from the subsystem equations, the proposed method improves prediction accuracy when only a limited number of snapshot pairs are available. We also demonstrate its effectiveness through numerical experiments on coupled oscillator systems.

title: A plant virus, TYLCV, up-regulates an endocrine oxylipin signal in its insect vector, Bemisia tabaci, via the viral C2 virulence factor for viral transmission
abstractText: Abstract Background Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is transmitted by Bemisia tabaci through a circulative and replicative pathway and must overcome vector immune defenses to achieve efficient transmission. Oxylipins are important regulators of insect immunity, in which eicosanoids generally promote antiviral responses whereas C18 epoxyoctadecamonoenoic acids (EpOMEs) act as immune suppressors. Although manipulation of insect immunity by plant viruses has been increasingly recognized, the molecular mechanisms by which TYLCV reshapes vector physiology to establish a permissive infection state remain poorly understood. Methodology TYLCV infection and localization in B. tabaci were analyzed using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), immunofluorescence assays (IFA), and quantitative PCR. Oxylipin functions were examined through oral delivery of prostaglandins, EpOMEs, pathway inhibitors, and lipid analogs. EpOME levels were quantified by LC–MS/MS. Candidate genes involved in eicosanoid and EpOME biosynthesis or degradation were predicted through bioinformatic and phylogenetic analyses and functionally evaluated using RNA interference (RNAi). Intestinal apoptosis was assessed using TUNEL and cleaved caspase-3 immunostaining. Immune-associated genes and viral determinants were investigated through RT-qPCR and gene-specific RNAi, including silencing of all six TYLCV genes. Results TYLCV progressively accumulated in the intestine of B. tabaci and significantly altered fatty acid metabolism. Two oxylipin pathways exerted antagonistic effects on viral accumulation. Prostaglandin E₂ (PGE₂) and its biosynthetic machinery, including BtPLA2-A, BtPLA2-C, Bt-PGES2, and Bt-PGE2R, functioned as antiviral regulators, whereas both EpOME isomers (9,10- and 12,13-EpOME) promoted viral accumulation. TYLCV infection elevated EpOME levels more than two-fold and transcriptionally favored EpOME accumulation by inducing Bt-CYP6 while suppressing Bt-sEH2 and Bt-sEH3 . Pharmacological and RNAi analyses confirmed Bt-CYP6 as an EpOME-associated synthase and Bt-sEH2/3 as degradation-associated genes. EpOME promoted intestinal apoptosis and selectively regulated immune-associated genes, inducing proviral factors including defensin and cathepsins while suppressing antiviral factors such as knottin and PGRP. Comparison of TYLCV strains revealed that the more virulent TYLCV-IL induced stronger EpOME signaling and apoptosis than TYLCV-Mld. Among all viral genes, only TYLCV-C2 controlled host EpOME machinery; silencing C2 abolished Bt-CYP6 induction and restored Bt-sEH2/3 expression, while exogenous EpOME rescued viral accumulation. Conclusion TYLCV exploits vector oxylipin signaling to establish a permissive physiological state in B. tabaci . Through the viral C2 factor, TYLCV shifts host signaling from an antiviral eicosanoid-dominant state toward a proviral EpOME-dominant state, thereby promoting apoptosis, reshaping immune responses, and enhancing viral accumulation and transmission potential.

title: Climate Resilience Engineering: Thermal Adaptations of the Nitrogenase Mo–Fe α Subunit for Sustainable Agriculture
abstractText: Abstract Increasing temperatures are a concern for global agriculture because they inhibit the activity of the nitrogenase enzyme, which is crucial for N2 fixation. The study reveals how the nitrogenase Mo–Fe α subunit adapts to high temperatures by comparing thermophilic and mesophilic bacteria. The molecular dynamics simulation study of Acetivibrio thermocellus and Endomicrobium proavitum explores how specific amino acids contribute to their physicochemical shifts, such as increased aliphatic index, hydrogen bonds, secondary-structure content, and decreased RMSD and RMSF, which reflect constrained conformational dynamics that confer thermal resilience. A. thermocellus maintains a more compact, stable structure under heat stress. These structural features enable the engineering of heat-tolerant nitrogenase, boosting sustainable agriculture in warm-climate regions.

title: A high-precision measurement method for ruby balls based on multi-scale adaptive edge detection
abstractText: Abstract This paper proposes a high-precision measurement method for ruby balls based on multi-scale adaptive edge detection. By combining dark field imaging technology with improved Canny algorithm, the accuracy and robustness of edge extraction have been significantly improved. When measuring 5mm ruby balls, the average absolute error of this method is only 1.6µm, which is about 66% lower than the Hessian matrix method and about 83% lower than the regionprops method; When the signal-to-noise ratio drops to 20 dB, the error growth only reaches 2.4m, while the traditional Canny algorithm reaches 6.5µm. For samples with different diameters (3-12mm) and materials (ruby, ceramic, hard alloy), the algorithm's measurement error is controlled within 0.2–0.3µm, and the repeatability is better than 0.15µm, meeting the micrometer level accuracy requirements of high-end manufacturing industry. The experiment verified the excellent adaptability and robustness of this method in complex environments.

title: China’s Consumption Geography: A County-level Estimation of Daily Consumption Using Big Data
abstractText: Abstract Residents’ daily consumption (RDC) levels provide an important indicator of regional development. However, existing research has largely examined consumption patterns either at coarse spatial scales or through localized case studies owing to data constraints, limiting our understanding of fine-grained spatial disparities in consumption. Using Baidu Population Profiling data, this study systematically examines the geography of RDC levels across county-level units in China and explores the socioeconomic factors underlying regional variation in consumption levels. We find that RDC levels exhibit pronounced east–west spatial disparities, with markedly higher RDC in coastal urban agglomerations. Regional RDC levels are closely associated with administrative levels and urbanization rate. A significant relationship can also be observed between urbanization and the upgrading of consumption structures. Both consumption market and consumption amenity play important roles in raising regional consumption levels. Improvements in consumption market primarily contribute to consumption upgrading by reducing the proportion of low-level consumption populations, whereas better consumption amenity is more strongly associated with an expansion of the high-level consumption population.

Prospective evaluation of automated KU F40 fecal analysis versus microscopy for intestinal protozoa and illustrative labor costs
abstractText: Abstract Stool ova-and-parasite (O&P) microscopy remains widely used but is labor-intensive and constrained by expert availability. AI-assisted automated fecal analyzers can digitize stool microscopy workflows and generate images that may support remote expert review; however, evaluations should distinguish algorithm-only output from clinically deployable workflows that incorporate human verification. In a prospective diagnostic study at a tertiary-care parasitology laboratory in Izmir, Türkiye (November 2024–October 2025), 1000 consecutive, unselected adult human stool specimens submitted for routine testing were assessed in parallel by routine microscopy and the KU-F40 automated fecal analyzer. All 1,000 specimens contributed paired entries to the analysis tables. KU-F40 was evaluated as automated diagnosis (AD; algorithm call before human review) and AD plus expert user verification (AD + UV; expert review of KU-F40-generated images). The diagnostic AD + UV analysis was kept distinct from the labor-cost model, which evaluated illustrative 30%-verification and universal-verification scenarios. Relative to routine microscopy, KU-F40 AD showed positive/negative percent agreement (PPA/NPA) of 100%/99.8% for Entamoeba histolytica/dispar , 100%/98.6% for Giardia spp ., and 67.3%/97.7% for Blastocystis spp. Expert verification removed the 14 microscopy-negative Giardia AD calls and reduced microscopy-negative Blastocystis calls from 22 to 12; the two microscopy-negative E. histolytica/dispar calls remained UV-supported but were not independently adjudicated. Coccidia ( Cryptosporidium spp., Cyclospora cayetanensis ) fell outside the KU-F40 classifier panel and were identified only by conventional microscopy. The illustrative labor model assumed 35 min/specimen for microscopy and 2 min/specimen for AD, with 10 min of specialist time per verified specimen; no formal time-and-motion study was performed. The resulting modeled direct labor costs (USD/specimen) for microscopy, AD and illustrative 30%-verification AD + UV were Türkiye 4.56/0.20/0.72, Germany 21.87/0.91/3.46 and UK 27.21/0.79/4.66. KU-F40 provided a digitized screening workflow. Under the specified assumptions, the illustrative labor model yielded lower estimated hands-on labor inputs and direct labor costs than conventional microscopy; these were model outputs, not observed operational performance. Expert verification improved agreement for selected organisms, but UV-supported discordant calls were not an independent confirmation of infection. KU-F40 did not cover Cryptosporidium or Cyclospora in this evaluation; conventional and dedicated methods therefore remain necessary whenever these organisms fall within the requested diagnostic scope. Multi-site studies with measured workflow times and independent discordance adjudication are required before implementation or cost-effectiveness claims.

title: Benchmarking hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for power grid optimization problems
abstractText: Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow Unit Commitment (AC-OPF-UC) is a difficult mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem that combines binary generator commitment decisions with nonconvex continuous AC power-flow constraints. In this work, we investigate whether hybrid quantum-classical variational algorithms can improve the solution of single-period AC-OPF-UC relative to classical approaches. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to directly evaluate quantum or hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for the full AC-OPF-UC problem. We consider two candidate algorithms for improving AC-OPF-UC solution quality relative to purely classical methods on ideal quantum hardware. The first applies QAOA directly to a fully discretized formulation of the problem, with equality and inequality constraints incorporated through penalty terms and slack variables. Although conceptually straightforward, this approach requires a prohibitively large number of qubits even for small instances. The second, qubit-efficient approach encodes only the binary generator status variables on a quantum computer, while optimizing the continuous power-flow variables classically for each sampled bitstring. We benchmark this method on randomly generated AC-OPF-UC instances with 5 to 13 generators and compare it against SCIP, SMAC, and uniform random sampling. Our simulations show that the qubit-efficient hybrid method does not outperform uniform sampling. These results suggest that in order to establish potential advantage of the variational hybrid strategy considered here over the best classical algorithms, if any, much larger system sizes (25+ generators) need to be tested, which is beyond our computational capacity. Alternatively, different approaches, such as quantum versions of branch-and-bound methods, may be more promising.

title: Probiotic mixture golden bifid attenuates dyslipidemia in obesity, reshapes gut microbiota, and downregulates FABP2 expression
abstractText: Abstract Background Our previous study demonstrated that fatty acid binding protein 2 (FABP2) expression was significantly upregulated in mice fed a high-fat diet (HFD). In the present study we evaluated the effects and therapeutic mechanisms of Golden Bifid, a probiotic mixture Bifidobacterium longum subsp. longum , Streptococcus salivarius subsp. thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus (BSL) on HFD-induced obesity and gut microbiota composition. Methods Male C57BL/6 mice were fed either a normal diet or an HFD. HFD-fed mice were orally administered saline or BSL by gavage. After 6 weeks of treatment, organ indices, blood lipid profiles, fasting blood glucose, gene expression, and gut microbiota composition were analyzed. Results BSL treatment reduced body weight gain, fasting blood glucose, and epididymal white adipose tissue mass, increased the brown adipose tissue index, and improved serum, fecal, and hepatic lipids profiles in HFD-induced obese mice. BSL also significantly altered the expression of genes involved in lipid metabolism and transport in the jejunum. Specifically, the mRNA expression levels of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)γ, FABP2, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMG-CoA reductase), and PPAR α were significantly decreased, whereas liver X receptor α (LXR-α) expression was significantly increased. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway analysis further showed that BSL suppressed fatty acid metabolism and the PPAR signaling pathway. In addition, BSL increased the relative abundance of Rikenellaceae , Bifidobacteriaceae , Barnesiella and Paramuribaculum , while decreasing that of Allobaculum , Blautia and Kribbibacteriaceae . Conclusion BSL improves obesity and obesity-associated lipid metabolism disorders, modulates gut microbiota, and inhibiting the expression of PPARγ, FABP2, HMG-CoA reductase and PPARα. title: Balancing O2 Consumption and Monomer Evaporation to Tune Alkene Polymerization in Protective Coatings
abstractText: Abstract Alkene resins with acrylate-based cross-linkers are widely used as coatings to protect metal surfaces from corrosion. Environmental and safety concerns are stimulating the replacement of resin components. Especially, replacing volatile reactive diluents (i.e., styrene) with less volatile diluents and the cobalt(II) carboxylates that activate the alkyl peroxide initiators with benign transition-metal catalysts (e.g., Fe(II) complexes) is desirable. Polymerization of thin coatings (ca. 50–300 μm, depending on the application) involves both physical and chemical processes, including evaporation of diluent, diffusion-driven compositional gradients, and continuous ingress and consumption of O2. In this report, we deconvolute the effects of monomer evaporation and O2 uptake/consumption in air-exposed resin films and show that the final composition of the film is determined by the relative rates of catalyzed O2 depletion and O2 uptake from air and the increase in viscosity due to evaporation of the diluent. The one-dimensional diffusion-reaction model developed for O2 penetration/consumption enables rational tuning of loading of the commercially relevant catalyst Fe(II)-bispidine to provide similar performance as with the industry-standard Co(II) catalysts.

title: State of Wildfires 2025–2026
abstractText: The global geography, behaviour, and impact of fires are shifting, as spatially varying human influences interact with a visibly changing climate. The State of Wildfires project systematically tracks global and regional fire activity, analyses the causes of prominent extreme wildfire events for three focal regions, and projects the likelihood of similar events under future climate scenarios. During the March 2025–February 2026 fire season, global burned area (BA) was 18 % below the 2002–2024 average and global fire carbon (C) emissions were also 20 %–31 % below average, making it one of the lowest years on record. Yet this globally low fire year still produced widespread regional impacts. Canada experienced a third consecutive extreme fire year, with national fire C emissions at nearly triple the average since 2002, 70 000 evacuations, and reported direct losses of USD 360 million. In the Midwestern Canadian Shield Forests, the epicentre of Canada's anomalous season, we find that anthropogenic climate change has nearly doubled (likely synthesis range 0.33–44.9, median 1.85) the likelihood of extreme fire weather in this region and made the observed BA around 10 times more likely during July–August 2025. BA extent in the region is found to be 9 times greater. Many parts of Europe also experienced record or high-ranking BA and fire C emissions, including in Spain, Portugal, and the UK, and a record USD 4.11 billion of physical assets were exposed to fire across the continent. Direct fatalities occurred in Türkiye (17), Spain (8), Portugal (6), Cyprus (2), Greece (1) and France (1), and evacuations in Türkiye, Spain, and Greece totalled over 110 000. In the Northwest Iberian Peninsula, we find that extreme fire weather over August 2025 was around 3 times (virtually certain modelled range 0.14–657, median 3.63) more likely due to climate change. Under a high-emissions scenario (SSP3-7.0), fires of the same return interval are likely to burn about 78 % more area by the end of the century, with some projections within the same scenario suggesting increases of around sevenfold. In Chile and northwest Argentina, January–February 2026 fires caused 23 fatalities, displaced 55 000 people and threatened a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the Chilean Temperate Forests and Matorral, the epicentre, we find that BA was around two times larger due to anthropogenic climate change. Across all focal regions in this report, the conditions for extreme fire developed gradually through months of precipitation deficits, cumulative drying and, in the case of Northwest Iberia, antecedent fuel accumulation aided by preceding wet periods. Continued climate change is expected to intensify these hydroclimatic extremes. However, comparison of SSP3-7.0 with SSP5-8.5 suggests that projected end-of-century extreme BA events in our focal regions are 4 %–23 % smaller than under the very high-emissions futures that were once considered plausible.. Meeting the Paris targets (SSP1-2.6) would further reduce BA during these events by 5 %–36 % across our focal regions. By integrating expertise from across the wildfire community with state-of-the-art observations, data, and modelling, this annual report advances understanding of regional wildfire extremes and their drivers, providing evidence to inform policy, preparedness, mitigation, adaptation, and broader societal benefit. Fifteen new and updated datasets created in this report are available from the State of Wildfires Project's Zenodo community (https://zenodo.org/communities/stateofwildfiresproject/, last access: 23 October 2026).

title: Crystal-field modulation activates dormant tetrahedral Co sites for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstractText: Water activation in the Volmer step is a major kinetic bottleneck in alkaline hydrogen evolution, yet the catalytic potential of many lattice sites remains underutilized. Here, we develop an oxalic-acid-assisted treatment to modulate the surface coordination environment of spinel Co3O4 while preserving its crystalline framework. The optimized U-Co3O4-2 electrode requires an overpotential of 19 mV to reach 10 mA cm-2 in 1.0 M KOH and sustains operation for at least 1000 h. Density functional theory indicates that coordination unsaturation reconstructs the local crystal field and selectively lowers dz2 occupation at tetrahedral Co sites. The resulting orbital redistribution reduces the population of Co–H2O antibonding states, strengthens Co–H2O coupling, and makes dissociative water activation thermodynamically more favorable. Thus, tetrahedral Co sites that are weakly active in pristine Co3O4 can be converted into catalytically competent water-activation centers. These results identify coordination-induced crystal-field modulation as a strategy for increasing lattice-site utilization in non-noble-metal alkaline HER catalysts.

title: Differences in knee isokinetic strength under experimentally controlled cervical forward-flexion movement in university soccer players: a within-participant study using wearable flexible strain sensors
abstractText: Abstract Background isokinetic strength testing is the international gold standard for quantitative muscle function assessment. However, the absence of standardized cervical positioning protocols introduces a critical confounding variable that compromises the validity of knee strength measurements. This study aimed to verify the impact of compensatory cervical forward flexion on knee isokinetic outcomes using wearable flexible strain sensors and to establish an evidence-based postural standardization protocol. Methods This self-controlled trial enrolled 39 university soccer players. A high-resolution wearable flexible strain sensor combined with self-developed computer software named Resistance Monitor was used to collect and process real-time angular data of the first to the seventh cervical vertebra, so as to quantify cervical forward flexion range of motion and identify flexion compensation patterns. Combined with the A8-2 isokinetic dynamometer, knee torque indicators including knee extensor and flexor relative peak torque, hamstring-to-quadriceps peak torque ratio, average peak torque and other primary measures were measured at 30°/s and 60°/s, whereas cervical forward flexion range of motion was assessed at 180°/s. All intergroup comparisons, correlation analyses and repeatability tests were performed using SPSS 27.0 and OriginPro 2025. Results Compensatory cervical forward flexion induced significant alterations in both extension and flexion parameters of right knee isokinetic assessments at 30°/s (all p < 0.01). At 60°/s, significant changes were only observed for right knee extension parameters (all p < 0.05), whereas flexion parameters remained unaffected (all p > 0.05). Bonferroni correction was applied for all statistical analyses in this study. At 180°/s, correlation analysis was conducted on simultaneously acquired cervical range of motion and relative resistance variation, yielding a Spearman’s ρ of 0.925 ( p < 0.001). Conclusions These findings demonstrate that cervical forward flexion compensation serves as an overlooked biomechanical confounder that systematically biases knee isokinetic extensor and flexor measurements. Consistent maintenance of cervical neutral positioning is recommended to eliminate this systematic bias. This work provides empirical foundation for postural standardization in knee isokinetic protocols and expands the translational application of the wearable flexible strain sensor in rehabilitative biomechanics and sports medicine. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, ChiCTR2600127415. (Current Controlled on June 11, 2026).

title: Cross-border disaster victim identification after the Struma Motorway bus fire: operational response and element-by-element comparison with the INTERPOL DVI Guide
abstractText: Abstract Background Mass-fatality road incidents with severely burned victims require integration of scene recovery, post-mortem examination, ante-mortem information and reconciliation. In the Struma Motorway bus fire in Bulgaria on 23 November 2021, all victims were nationals of the neighbouring country. This report presents the findings from all 45 decedents, describes the local workflow assembled out of necessity, and compares it element by element with the INTERPOL Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) Guide. It is a retrospective review of the judicially mandated medico-legal investigation, based on the scene, autopsy, toxicology and DNA records, the ante-mortem material from North Macedonia and the identification outcomes. Carboxyhemoglobin and recovery position were transcribed from the annotated scene schematic, and 33 Guide elements were extracted before scoring and assigned one of five descriptors, from fulfilled to not fulfilled. Results The first search did not clear all compartments of the vehicle; when reconciliation showed one passenger unaccounted for, a repeat examination recovered the 45th decedent, a child, from a luggage hold. DNA profiles from all 45 sets of remains were compared with those of 34 relatives sampled in North Macedonia; DNA and dental analysis resolved a dizygotic twin pair and two sibling groups. All 45 victims were identified within 10 days. The certified cause of death was fatal thermal injury in all 45; a vital injury not attributable to heat was found in one. Carboxyhemoglobin was not detected in seven decedents and reached 49%, increasing from front to rear (zone medians 9%, 16%, 23%). Of 33 Guide elements, 17 were fulfilled by a documented local equivalent, 10 with partial documentation and 1 was not fulfilled; 2 were not applicable and 3 remain to be put in place. Conclusions Assembled in hours because no standing DVI team existed, the response identified all victims, with two documented shortfalls: an incomplete first search and a numbering convention that differed between two scene documents. Transferable elements are early cross-border collection of ante-mortem material, parallel post-mortem workstreams, reconciliation empowered to reopen a closed phase, and strict enforcement of the primary-identifier hierarchy. Foremost to prepare in advance is a trained national DVI team.

title: Ibogalogs reduce acute and chronic headache-like behaviours in rodents by mechanisms involving both 5-HT1 and 5-HT2 receptor subtypes
abstractText: Abstract The main objective of this work is to assess whether ibogalogs decrease headache-like behaviors in rats using the cortical spreading depression (CSD) and medication overuse headache (MOH) models. The CSD and MOH results showed that tabernanthalog (TBG), ibogainalog (IBG), and ibogaminalog (DM506) significantly decreased allodynia induced by acute injection of KCl or repetitive administration of sumatriptan. The effect of ibogalogs in the CSD model was sex-independent. The observed effects lasted 6–8 h, with TBG showing comparatively higher efficacy in both models. We also assessed the potential role of serotonin type 2 receptor (5-HT 2 R) and 5-HT 1B/1D R subtypes the effects of ibogalogs using selective antagonists such as ketanserin and GR127935, respectively. The antagonist effects were headache type-dependent: in acute headache, GR127935 inhibited ibogalogs’ activity during the first hour but subsequently enhanced their effects, whereas ketanserin enhanced their activities; in chronic headache, GR127935 abolished ibogalog’s effects during the first 3 h, whereas ketanserin inhibited IBG’s effect during the first 2 h but enhanced TBG’s effect. These results suggested that the antiheadache effects of ibogalogs are mediated by co-modulation of 5-HT 1 R and 5-HT 2 R subtypes. The functional results showed the ibogalogs activate 5-HT 1 R subtypes with the following selectivity: 5-HT 1F R ~ 5-HT 1D R > 5-HT 1B R > > 5-HT 1E R. Thus, we compared the activity of ibogalogs between wild type (WT) and 5-HT 1F R knockout (KO) mice in the MOH model. The results in WT mice showed that ibogalogs increase the facial withdrawal threshold with the following efficacy: TBG > IBG > DM506. Moreover, ibogalog antiallodynic effects were reduced in KO mice after 4 h, supporting a role for the 5-HT 1F R in the actions of ibogalogs in headache attenuation. In conclusion, ibogalogs significantly reduce acute and chronic headache-like behaviors by a co-modulatory mechanism between 5-HT 1 R and 5-HT 2 R subtypes.

title: Tinjauan Literatur: Faktor-Faktor yang Mempengaruhi Keterikatan Karyawan di Era Digital
abstractText: Studi ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi berbagai elemen yang memengaruhi keterlibatan karyawan employee engagement di era digital. Masalah difokuskan pada perubahan lingkungan kerja akibat transformasi digital. Kajian ini menggunakan teori Job Demands-Resources dan Self-Determination Theory. Melalui studi pustaka pada berbagai artikel ilmiah yang relevan serta analisis kualitatif, temuan penelitian ini mengindikasikan bahwa employee engagement dipengaruhi oleh digital leadership, digital work environment, digital literacy, employee well-being, meaningful work, dan motivation. Transformasi digital dapat meningkatkan keterikatan karyawan apabila didukung kepemimpinan yang baik, lingkungan kerja yang sehat, kemampuan digital, kesejahteraan, kebermaknaan kerja, dan motivasi. Sebaliknya, tuntutan digital yang tidak diimbangi dukungan organisasi dapat menimbulkan tekanan kerja. Kajian ini menyimpulkan bahwa organisasi perlu mengelola aspek teknologi dan manusia secara seimbang untuk meningkatkan keterikatan karyawan di era digital.

title: Increased frequency of dislocation following total hip arthroplasty for trauma
abstractText: Aims The purpose of this study was to compare surgical techniques and postoperative outcomes in an age- and sex-matched cohort of patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) for neck of femur fracture (#NOF) and for osteoarthritis (OA). Methods A single-centre, consecutive series of patients at minimum one-year follow-up following THA for #NOF were compared with a 1:1 age- and sex-matched cohort of patients following THA for osteoarthritis from the same institution. The primary outcome measure was frequency of dislocation at one year postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included rates of all-cause revision, infection, periprosthetic fracture, and mortality at one year and medium-term postoperatively. Cox regression compared medium-term outcomes between groups, accounting for unequal follow-up duration. Results A total of 722 patients were included, with 361 in each group. BMI was greater in the OA group (28.9 kg/m 2 vs 24.7 kg/m 2 ; p < 0.001). Sex, age, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, and comorbidity profile did not differ between groups (p > 0.247). Overall, 151 patients (41.8%) in the #NOF group received dual-mobility implants, compared with eight (2.2%) in the OA group (p < 0.001). Femoral offset was similar between groups (42.6 mm and 42.7 mm, p = 0.892). Dislocation rates were greater in the #NOF group than the OA group at one-year (4.4% vs 1.1%; p = 0.011) and by final follow-up. The one-year rates of periprosthetic fracture, all-cause revision, and mortality were similar between groups (p > 0.340), although risk of mortality was greater by final follow-up after THA for #NOF (hazard ratio 1.577; p = 0.033). Conclusion Despite the more frequent use of dual-mobility implants in THA for #NOF than OA and the otherwise comparable patient demographics and implants used, the risk of early dislocation after THA for #NOF was four times greater than in an age- and sex-matched elective THA cohort. Early postoperative complication rates were otherwise comparable between the groups. Cite this article: Bone Jt Open 2026;7(11):1455–1461.

Group Counseling Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques to Improve Self-Confidence in Students Experiencing Body Image Dissatisfaction
abstractText: This study aims to systematically examine the implementation of cognitive restructuring techniques in group counseling to enhance secondary school students’ self-confidence, investigate the relationship between body image dissatisfaction and self-confidence, and identify factors influencing counseling outcomes. A qualitative Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted using the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and SPIDER framework. Relevant publications from 2017 to 2026 were retrieved through Google Scholar and GARUDA. Ten primary studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising seven intervention studies and three correlational studies. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, followed by thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that cognitive restructuring generally involves identifying negative thoughts, developing rational alternatives, practicing positive self-statements, and evaluating behavioral changes. Intervention studies consistently reported improvements in students’ self-confidence, although methodological limitations restrict causal conclusions. Student participation and supportive environments facilitated implementation, whereas embarrassment, hesitation, and fear of criticism constituted barriers. Correlational studies demonstrated significant positive relationships between body image and self-confidence without establishing causality. Importantly, none of the reviewed intervention studies specifically examined students experiencing body image dissatisfaction. This review contributes by integrating previously separate research findings and identifying an important evidence gap. Further controlled studies are recommended to evaluate cognitive restructuring interventions specifically among students experiencing body image dissatisfaction.

abstractText: Pengendalian dan otomatisasi beban penerangan listrik pada fasilitas gedung pendidikan merupakan salah satu langkah efektif efisiensi energi. Gedung B Universitas Teknologi Ronggolawe Cepu sebelumnya mengoperasikan beban listrik secara manual menggunakan saklar konvensional, sehingga penggunaan energi kurang terkontrol dan memicu pemborosan. title: Assessing outcomes and recovery following anterior cervical discectomy and fusion in patients aged 75 years and older: a propensity score–matched review with 2-year follow-up
abstractText: OBJECTIVE The longitudinal efficacy of anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) in the population of older individuals is debated. The authors aimed to determine the long-term outcomes of patients aged ≥ 75 years compared to those of their younger peers. METHODS A prospectively collected quality registry of patients undergoing elective ACDF was retrospectively reviewed. Cohorts included patients who were ≥ 75 years compared to < 75 years of age. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were collected at baseline and 3, 12, and 24 months postoperatively. Demographics, surgical characteristics, complications, Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10) dysphagia rates, North American Spine Society satisfaction, and PROMs were compared between groups. All analyses were repeated following 1:1 propensity score matching by demographics, baseline PROMs, comorbidities, symptoms, and surgical factors. RESULTS A total of 1155 patients met inclusion criteria with 1082 (94%) aged < 75 years and 73 (6%) ≥ 75 years. Prior to propensity score matching, the ≥ 75-year cohort had a lower mean BMI (29.0 ± 4.3 vs 30.9 ± 6.6 kg/m 2 , p = 0.028), fewer daily smokers (4.1% vs 16%, p = 0.005), fewer currently employed workers (5.5% vs 52%, p < 0.001), and lower rates of anxiety (15% vs 28%, p = 0.017) and depression (12% vs 23%, p = 0.041). The ≥ 75-year cohort had more osteoarthritis (47% vs 24%, p < 0.001) and coronary artery disease (23% vs 6.5%, p < 0.001). The ≥ 75-year cohort had significantly better neck pain visual analog scale, arm pain visual analog scale (AP-VAS), Neck Disability Index, EuroQol 5-Dimension, and EuroQol visual analog scale baseline scores (all p < 0.05), but similar modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scores (p = 0.2). By the 2-year follow-up, all PROM scores were similar except for the AP-VAS score, for which the ≥ 75-year cohort reported less arm pain (1.2 ± 2.5 vs 1.7 ± 2.7, p = 0.044). Propensity score matching yielded 138 patients, with 69 in each cohort. Residual demographic differences included the ≥ 75-year cohort having fewer employed workers (5.8% vs 42%, p < 0.001) and more individuals with a professional degree (25% vs 8.7%, p = 0.012). The propensity score–matched cohorts achieved parity in all baseline, postoperative, and change-from-baseline PROM scores through the 2-year follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Patients aged ≥ 75 years experience benefit comparable to that of younger patients across outcome measures following propensity score matching. Age alone does not predict worsened outcomes in carefully selected older patients undergoing elective ACDF, and older patients may benefit from knowledge of comparable favorable outcomes.

title: O ENSINO COLABORATIVO COMO APOIO À INCLUSÃO ESCOLAR: POTENCIALIDADES, PRÁTICAS DE SUCESSO E DESAFIOS DE IMPLEMENTAÇÃO
abstractText: Este artigo analisa o ensino colaborativo (coensino) como estratégia para a efetivação da inclusão escolar no Brasil. Por meio de revisão sistemática e integrativa da literatura produzida entre 2010 e 2024, o estudo examina as potencialidades dessa abordagem pedagógica, identificando práticas bem-sucedidas em contextos educacionais distintos. A fundamentação teórica ancora-se em autores nacionais e internacionais de referência, discutindo a transição do modelo de suporte segregado para uma cultura de corresponsabilidade no espaço da sala de aula comum. Examinam-se os modelos de organização da bidocência, os estágios de desenvolvimento da parceria docente e os saberes necessários à colaboração eficaz. Discute-se, ainda, o papel estratégico da gestão escolar na institucionalização da prática e o potencial do coensino como indutor de formação continuada em serviço. Por fim, analisam-se os desafios estruturais e culturais à implementação em larga escala. Conclui-se que o ensino colaborativo representa uma mudança paradigmática necessária para superar a inclusão restrita à matrícula e assegurar o direito à aprendizagem e à participação plena de todos os estudantes na escola regular.

title: Structural and Photoluminescence Properties of Ba3Y1– z Lu z Al2O7.5: Bi3+/Bi3+,Eu3+ Phosphors for WLEDs Applications
abstractText: Abstract Bi3+-doped and Bi3+/Eu3+-codoped Ba3Y1–zLuzAl2O7.5 phosphors with different compositions were prepared via a high-temperature solid-state route, followed by systematic evaluation of their crystal structure, luminescence characteristics, energy transfer process, and temperature-dependent emission behavior. Under 323 nm near-ultraviolet excitation, Ba3YAl2O7.5: Bi3+ exhibits a broad yellow emission centered at 555 nm. Upon Eu3+ codoping, characteristic orange-red Eu3+ emission is introduced, producing a broad emission band spanning approximately 550–750 nm. Spectral overlap and fluorescence lifetime measurements confirm energy transfer from Bi3+ to Eu3+, with a maximum transfer efficiency of 35.66% at 7% Eu3+. Partial substitution of Y3+ by Lu3+ provides effective regulation of the local crystal environment. With increasing Lu3+ content, the Bi3+ emission peak gradually red-shifts from 555 to 577 nm, accompanied by improved thermal stability. For the optimized Ba3Y0.5Lu0.5Al2O7.5:2% Bi3+,3% Eu3+ phosphor, the Bi3+ and Eu3+ emission intensities retain 76% and 72% of their room-temperature values at 423 K, respectively. By combining the optimized phosphor with a commercial blue-emitting phosphor and a near-ultraviolet LED chip, a WLED was constructed, delivering an Ra value of 87 and a CCT of 4822 K. Moreover, the device maintains a largely unchanged spectral profile from 300 to 425 K. These results demonstrate that the combined Bi3+→Eu3+ energy transfer and Lu3+-substitution strategies provide an effective route for color tuning and thermal-stability improvement in phosphors for high-quality white-light applications.

title: The Effectiveness of Game-Based Simulation and Rapid Prototyping in Project-Based Learning on Students’ Understanding and Kinematics Problem-Solving Skills
abstractText: Physics learning requires students to interpret physical meaning and apply kinematics concepts in contextual situations. This study examined initial changes in students’ cognitive achievement following the integration of Game-Based Simulation and Rapid Prototyping into Project-Based Learning (PjBL). A quantitative pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design involved 92 Grade X students from three senior high schools in Kerinci Regency, Indonesia. Data comprised a five-item multiple-choice cognitive test administered before and after instruction and three four-point Likert questionnaires on perceived conceptual understanding, perceived problem-solving experience, and student response. The mean cognitive score increased from 40.22 to 89.35 (gain = 49.13; N-Gain = 0.841). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated a statistically significant pretest–posttest difference (p < 0.001; r = 0.868). At the indicator level, the largest increase was in motion representation/velocity–time relationships (+82.61 percentage points), followed by distance calculation (+72.83 points) and travel-time/fastest-route analysis (+59.78 points). Questionnaire averages were 90.99% for perceived conceptual understanding, 88.62% for perceived problem-solving experience, and 94.34% for student response. The questionnaire results represent students’ self-reported perceptions, not direct evidence of problem-solving performance. Because the study had no control group and the cognitive test contained only five items with low internal consistency, interpret the findings as preliminary evidence of improvement and confirm them with stronger designs and validated instruments. Keywords: game-based simulation, rapid prototyping, project-based learning, conceptual understanding, perceived problem-solving, kinematics.

Holey Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanofiltration Membranes: Microstructure–Transport Relations and Enhanced Fractionation of Complex Streams
abstractText: Abstract Membranes based on two-dimensional nanomaterials such as graphene oxide (GO) and reduced GO (rGO) are increasingly investigated for nanofiltration applications involving complex biomass-derived streams. However, GO membrane performance is limited by extended transport pathways and restricted flux arising from the tortuous alignment of impermeable nanosheets. We report a systematic study of reduced “holey” graphene oxide (rhGO) membranes, fabricated by controlled oxidative etching of GO nanosheets, to investigate the effect of in-plane nanopores on water and solute transport. Membranes with varying degrees of hole sizes and densities, as well as two distinct film thicknesses (70 and 130 nm), were evaluated systematically for pure water permeation and rejection of ionized and neutral solutes. Concurrently, the microstructural features of the nanoflakes and membranes (hole size distribution, flake size distribution) were characterized quantitatively with extensive AFM and TEM statistical measurements. The membrane permeation and microstructural data allowed the parametrization and validation of an extended transport model that allows the prediction of flux and solute rejection trends that account for the presence of holes in the membranes. Compared to nonholey rGO membrane controls, rhGO membranes demonstrated enhanced water flux and 3-fold increase in throughput during nanofiltration of a complex feedstock (kraft black liquor) while maintaining high lignin rejection (>95%) and similar divalent salt exclusion as nonholey rGO membranes. This study underscores the potential of nanosheet defect engineering as a scalable strategy for tuning microstructure–transport relationships in 2D-material-based membranes for harsh-environment separations.

Assessing Total Heat Load as a Proxy for Optimising Operating Specifications in Extractive Distillation
abstractText: Abstract In this work, it is assessed whether the total heat load of the two-column extractive distillation system is a useful proxy for determining the optimal number of stages in systems that use cooling water in the condensers and steam in the reboilers. Thereafter, the optimal operating specifications of the extractive distillation column must be updated accordingly. The heuristic method features a straightforward, sequential, iterative optimisation approach for theoretical designs of a two-column extractive distillation sequence, developed using a process simulator. Four case studies are optimised to demonstrate the methodology’s suitability. The results were compared against simulated annealing, full total annual cost sweeps and data available in the literature. In all four cases, the proxy guided the choice of reflux ratio, and total annual cost determined the stage count. The operating specifications were then refined. Essentially, the proxy is utilised to identify the trend in total annual cost with the stage number of the extractive distillation column; therefore, the location or region where the optimal number of stages exists can be rapidly identified. Due to its efficiency, the proposed approach can theoretically be utilised to determine the optimal system specifications, using more complex modelling approaches, such as rate-based simulations.

title: The coping strategies used by university students with physical disabilities in managing psychological challenges in Tanzania
abstractText: University Students with Physical Disabilities (USPDs) often experience stress, anxiety, and depression arising from academic, social, and environmental barriers. This study examined the coping strategies USPDs use to manage psychological challenges in selected universities in Morogoro Region, Tanzania. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed. Purposive and snowball sampling recruited 74 students. Quantitative data were collected through questionnaires, including an adapted Brief COPE inventory, and analysed in SPSS using descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, and hierarchical multiple regression. Qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and analysed thematically. USPDs used emotion-focused coping significantly more than problem-focused coping (M = 19.43, SD = 3.95 vs. M = 13.97, SD = 3.85), t(73) = 7.67, p < .001, d = 0.89. Registration with disability support services was the only significant predictor of problem-focused coping, explaining an additional 11.2% of variance after controlling for demographic characteristics and disability severity. Residence was the only significant predictor of emotion-focused coping, with off-campus students scoring lower; interviews did not explain this association, and its cause cannot be established in a cross-sectional design. Common emotion-focused strategies included breathing exercises, sharing with peers, entertainment, and spiritual practices. Problem-focused strategies, such as task management and seeking academic support, were less frequent because many stressors were perceived as beyond students’ control. Limited institutional support encouraged temporary avoidance responses, such as ignoring, to regulate emotions. The study concludes that strengthening disability support services and inclusive learning environments may promote adaptive coping and psychological well-being among USPDs.

Enhanced Propane Dehydroaromatization over CeZn/ZSM-5 Nanosheets
abstractText: Abstract Propane dehydroaromatization (PDA) provides an efficient nonpetroleum route for upgrading light alkanes into high-value aromatics, yet conventional Zn-modified ZSM-5 (Zn/n-HZSM-5) catalysts suffer from rapid deactivation owing to diffusion limitations and subsequent carbon deposition. Herein, we developed a catalyst with a shortened b-axis (Zn/s-HZSM-5) via a urea-assisted hydrothermal method to optimize mass transfer within the zeolite channels. Compared with the Zn/n-HZSM-5 possessing a prolonged b-axis thickness of 250–270 nm, the Zn/s-HZSM-5 catalyst exhibited a significantly thinner b-axis of 100–130 nm, leading to a dramatic enhancement in propane conversion from 39.5% to 89.1%. Zero-length column (ZLC) desorption, fixed-bed breakthrough, and transient propane/N2 switching experiments demonstrated that the shortened b-axis pathways accelerated the diffusion of heavy aromatics, thereby reducing their residence time within the micropores. Ultraviolet Raman (UV-Raman) and thermogravimetric (TG) analyses revealed that Zn/s-HZSM-5 suppresses graphitic coke formation, which was responsible for irreversible pore-mouth blocking. To improve the regeneration durability of the catalyst, a trace amount of Ce was incorporated (0.10CeZn/s-HZSM-5), giving an aromatics yield exceeding 50% after three consecutive reaction–regeneration cycles (560 °C, WHSV at 0.8 h–1 and N2/C3H8 at 1.5 vol/vol). This work indicates that managing diffusion kinetics via b-axis manipulation is a key strategy for achieving sustained longevity in alkane upgrading.

Adolescent Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Can Be the First Clue to Multisystem Mitochondrial Disease
abstractText: Up to 40% of children with mitochondrial disease develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) during their disease course, but HCM is almost never the first presenting manifestation. When it is, the underlying mitochondrial disorder is easily missed: the cardiomyopathy is managed in isolation, and extracardiac findings that emerge later may be dismissed as unrelated. We describe an adolescent whose severe HCM was the first major manifestation of clinicopathologically confirmed multisystem mitochondrial disease with a phenotype consistent with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy. Her cardiomyopathy was managed in isolation for over a year before optic atrophy, primary ovarian insufficiency, osteopenia, and exercise intolerance were ultimately recognized as part of a single mitochondrial process. Endomyocardial and skeletal muscle biopsy confirmed mitochondrial pathology. The diagnosis directly changed management: cofactor supplementation was initiated, her visual acuity stabilized on idebenone, and perioperative planning for transplantation was adapted to prevent catabolic decompensation. Her cardiac disease progressed to heart failure requiring transplantation at age 16 years, but she remains clinically stable with preserved graft function more than 15 years later. This case challenges the assumption that mitochondrial disease should enter the differential only after neurologic dysfunction appears. General pediatricians, who see the whole child longitudinally, are uniquely positioned to recognize when dysfunction in other high-energy tissues points toward a unifying mitochondrial diagnosis in a child with cardiomyopathy.

Same Pressure, Different Outcomes? Land-System Change and the Divergence of Water Quality in São Paulo State (Brazil) and Europe
abstractText: Abstract Evidence that land-use change degrades surface water comes almost entirely from single-jurisdiction studies, which cannot ask whether the same land-system pressure is associated with the same water-quality outcome elsewhere. This study combines 41 years of annual MapBiomas land-cover data for six monitored water-management units (UGRHIs) in São Paulo State, Brazil, with a harmonised land-cover and water-quality panel for 179 European NUTS2 regions (LUCAS, cross-checked against Corine Land Cover for 2018, $$r=0.92$$ ). A within/between panel decomposition shows that within-unit increases in artificial land share are associated with lower nitrate (NO 3 –N) in São Paulo ( $$\beta =-0.210$$ standard deviations per percentage point, mixed-model $$p<0.001$$ ) and essentially unrelated to nitrate in Europe ( $$\beta =0.004$$ , 95% CI $$-0.026$$ to 0.034). The São Paulo estimate is stable across data-handling choices and precipitation adjustment, but it is not significant under cluster-robust or wild-cluster-bootstrap inference with six clusters ( $$p=0.23$$ and 0.43) or under a time-series-preserving permutation test ( $$p=0.30$$ ); it disappears when one unit is omitted, when unit-specific trends are allowed, and when land cover is measured over each station’s upstream drainage area ( $$\beta =-0.027$$ ). Biochemical oxygen demand and total phosphorus show no reliable within-unit differences, turbidity is associated with land use only in an exploratory model and not under few-cluster inference, and lead was excluded because its decline coincides with Brazil’s leaded-gasoline phase-out. The associations therefore differ across these monitored samples at the scale of management units, but their robustness and causes remain uncertain; differences in wastewater treatment are a plausible but untested explanation.

Rancang Bangun Aplikasi Perpustakaan Sekolah Berbasis Android Di SMK Negeri 07 Kota Bengkulu
abstractText: Current advancements in information technology are driving the transformation of school library management systems from conventional methods to digital-based systems. To date, SMK Negeri 07 Bengkulu City still employs a manual recording system for managing book collections, member data, and loan/return transactions. This situation carries the risk of recording errors and data loss, while also resulting in low operational efficiency. This study aims to design and develop an Android-based school library application to enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, and accessibility of library management. The system development method employed is the Waterfall model, comprising five key stages: requirements analysis, system design, code implementation, testing, and maintenance. The application was developed using the WebView-based Median.co platform, featuring an interactive web interface optimized for Android mobile devices. Research results indicate that the developed application facilitates book searches, member data recording, and library transactions through a computerized, real-time process. Black-box testing revealed a 100% success rate across all tested functional scenarios. Furthermore, questionnaire data from 32 respondents—analyzed using SPSS via the Pearson Product-Moment correlation test—showed an r-calculated value exceeding the r-table value (0.349) and a p-value of less than 0.001. Consequently, the application is deemed highly suitable, valid, and effective for implementation at SMK Negeri 07 Bengkulu City.

title: A model-driven framework for generating and classifying forage indicators and relationships to environmental conditions in Chesapeake Bay
ANALISIS PERFORMA MODEL CNN MELALUI EVALUASI EKSTERNAL PADA SISTEM KLASIFIKASI CITRA MAMMOGRAFI BERBASIS WEBSITE LOKAL
abstractText: The performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for mammographic image classification needs to be evaluated using data that were not involved in model development to assess its ability to generalize to data from different sources. This study aims to analyze the performance of a CNN model through external evaluation on a local web-based mammographic image classification system. The method involved applying the previously developed EfficientNetB2 model to 15 clinical mammographic images as external data. Each image was entered into the system to obtain its classification result, which was then compared with the diagnostic label in the original data. During the model development stage, the EfficientNetB2 model achieved an accuracy of 72%, precision of 67%, recall of 96% and an F1-score of 79%. The external evaluation results showed that 13 out of 15 images produced predictions consistent with their diagnostic labels, while 2 images produced inconsistent predictions, resulting in a prediction agreement rate of 86.67%. Based on the confusion matrix, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.67%, precision of 80%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 88.89%. The external evaluation provides an overview of the model’s generalization capability when applied to data outside its development environment through a local web-based system.

title: Green Human Resource Management and Environmentally Friendly Behavior of Employees in Iraq's Ministry of Environment
abstractText: Purpose: This study examines how Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), expressed through green recruitment, green training, green performance appraisal, and green rewards, relates to and influences the environmentally friendly behavior of employees at the Ministry of Environment in Baghdad, Iraq. Methodology: A descriptive analytical design was used. A questionnaire built on a five point Likert scale was distributed electronically to a convenience sample of 110 employees, and 98 questionnaires were returned. Validity was checked with Pearson item correlations, reliability with Cronbach's alpha, and the hypotheses were tested with Pearson correlation and simple linear regression in SPSS version 27. Results: All four GHRM dimensions were rated highly, with green performance appraisal ranked first. GHRM correlated strongly and positively with environmentally friendly behavior (r=0.673) and had a significant effect on it (B=0.752, F=77.079, R²=0.453). Green training and green rewards were the strongest individual dimensions. Conclusions: Green HR practices, particularly training and rewards, give the ministry a practical way to steer employees toward greener behavior at work. Limitations: The study relied on a single public organization, a small convenience sample, cross sectional self reported data, and bivariate analysis. Contributions: The study adds evidence from an Iraqi public sector setting, where GHRM research is still scarce, and offers managers concrete steps such as environmentally oriented job descriptions and incentives for employees who propose ways to reduce waste.

Formação de Professores, Ensino Colaborativo e Atendimento a Estudantes com Altas Habilidades ou Superdotação no Ensino Fundamental II
abstractText: Este estudo tem como objetivo analisar a formação de professores na Educação Básica, com ênfase no Ensino Fundamental II, e suas relações com o ensino colaborativo no atendimento a estudantes com altas habilidades ou superdotação (AH/SD). Parte-se da compreensão de que a organização do trabalho pedagógico, na perspectiva da educação inclusiva, envolve diferentes formas de articulação entre os docentes da sala comum e os profissionais do Atendimento Educacional Especializado. Como procedimento metodológico, realizou-se uma pesquisa bibliográfica e documental, de natureza qualitativa, fundamentada em produções acadêmicas brasileiras sobre formação docente, educação especial e AH/SD, complementada pela análise dos Projetos Pedagógicos de Curso e das ementas de dezoito campi de nove universidades públicas do Paraná, a fim de identificar se as matrizes curriculares contemplam essa temática. Os resultados indicam que a formação inicial de professores apresenta limitações no tratamento das especificidades da educação especial, sobretudo quanto às AH/SD, cuja presença nos currículos permanece restrita apesar do arcabouço legal consolidado desde a LDB até as diretrizes mais recentes para a formação docente. O ensino colaborativo aparece nas produções analisadas como possibilidade concreta de articulação pedagógica, ainda que sua presença seja incipiente nos debates sobre formação. Conclui-se que é necessária a ampliação das discussões sobre formação docente, inclusão escolar e organização do trabalho pedagógico, de modo a fortalecer práticas colaborativas mais consistentes no cotidiano escolar.
