Improved Hybrid DBN-HEVA Framework for Accurate Prediction and Multi-Objective Optimization of Die Sinking EDM Performance
abstractText: Electrical discharge machining (EDM) has made it possible to cut conductive metals that are either uncut or difficult to cut using standard machining techniques. In this EDM process, an accurate and flexible prediction and optimization model is required to evaluate this process and increase machining efficiency and surface quality. This study develops a novel adaptation of an improved Attention-Guided Deep Belief Network integrated with an Adaptive Human Eye Vision Algorithm (AG-DBN-AHEVA) for accurate prediction of EDM performance characteristics. Using an experimental dataset of 81 runs for accurate performance prediction, this work also examines the impact of EDM input parameters on material removal rate (MRR), tool wear rate (TWR), and Surface roughness (SR). To ensure high data quality and better generalization capability, pre-processing techniques including outlier detection, normalization, correlation analysis, and SMOTE-based regression augmentation were applied. The results showed that the suggested model outperformed the existing models, achieving the lowest prediction errors (MAE [Formula: see text] 0.007, RMSE [Formula: see text] 0.010) and the greatest [Formula: see text] value of 0.994. Furthermore, to attain the most effective EDM performance, multi-objective African Vultures Optimization is used to optimize MRR while decreasing TWR and SR. The ablation experiment, which demonstrates that the proposed model achieves higher prediction accuracy when compared to its reduced equivalents, justifies the inclusion of each component in the final design. Overall, this study demonstrated that the intelligent methodology proposed is a dependable, comprehensible, and highly effective AI-based approach for modeling and optimizing intelligent EDM processes in a high-technology manufacturing scenario.

Multi-Barrel Nanopipets as a Model System for Quantifying Interpore Interactions and Superadditive Transport
abstractText: Abstract Developing advanced neuromorphic ionic devices requires a quantitative understanding of how neighboring nanopores interact within arrays. Crosstalk between adjacent pores is especially important because overlapping depletion zones can suppress current and cause the current through a parallel-pore array to be lower than the sum of currents through isolated pores. Here, using dual-barrel nanopipets as a model two-pore array, we show that interacting barrels connected in parallel can also produce superadditive transport, where the combined current exceeds the sum of currents through two independently measured barrels. Conductance enhancement is observed when closely spaced barrels carry opposite surface charges, with one barrel negatively charged and the other positively charged. Poisson–Nernst–Planck and Navier–Stokes continuum modeling further clarifies the role of ion concentration polarization. The models indicate that applying voltage across neighboring, oppositely charged pores creates an ion-enriched zone at the entrance of one barrel that feeds the depletion zone at the entrance of the second barrel, thereby mitigating ion concentration polarization and increasing the combined conductance. These experiments and models advance understanding of electrically and chemically addressable, interacting nanopores for future ionic circuits.

COL4A1 mutation underlying recurrent spontaneous intraparenchymal hemorrhage in an adolescent: illustrative case
abstractText: BACKGROUND COL4A1 -associated vasculopathy is a rare genetic small-vessel disorder characterized by structural fragility of the cerebral vasculature and an increased risk of ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, and leukoaraiosis. Its implications for acute neurocritical care management remain incompletely defined. OBSERVATIONS An 18-year-old male with a prior history of unexplained intracerebral hemorrhage and diffuse cerebral microhemorrhages presented 1 year later with acute neurological deterioration due to a large cerebellar hemorrhage, requiring emergency external ventricular drain placement and suboccipital decompressive craniectomy. Extensive imaging, vascular, infectious, and inflammatory evaluations were unrevealing. During hospitalization, he experienced recurrent intracranial hemorrhages, including a pontine hemorrhage, out of proportion with underlying coagulopathy. Following initiation of pharmacological deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis, an additional hemorrhagic event occurred. Genetic testing ultimately revealed a pathogenic heterozygous COL4A1 mutation. LESSONS COL4A1 -associated disease should be considered in young patients with recurrent or unexplained intracranial hemorrhage and extensive cerebral microbleeds. Early recognition is critical, as standard neurocritical care algorithms including pharmacological thromboprophylaxis may confer increased hemorrhagic risk in the setting of diffuse structural vessel fragility. When identified early, genetic diagnosis should prompt proactive awareness of rebleeding risk and prospective modification of DVT prophylaxis timing and blood pressure targets rather than rigid application of standard ICH guidelines. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26379

title: Characterization of the vaginal microbiota of dairy cows treated with probiotics
abstractText: Abstract Approximately 50% of dairy cows develop postpartum uterine diseases, significantly affecting reproductive performance and economic returns. Treatment is usually based on antibiotics; however, alternative approaches have been investigated. This study evaluated the effects of intravaginal supplementation with lactic acid bacteria (LAB) on the vaginal microenvironment, focusing on microbial viability, pH, and taxonomic composition. A total of 21 non-pregnant, multiparous and non-lactating Jersey cows with synchronized estrous cycle were used. Animals were randomly assigned to two groups: Probiotic group (PRO; n = 11) received two intravaginal capsules containing Lactobacillus rhamnosus and Lactobacillus reuteri at 4.5 × 10¹⁰ CFU/capsule; and Control group (CTR; n = 10), receiving two intravaginal capsules without LAB. The recovery of Lactobacillus rhamnosus was significantly higher in the PRO group ( p < 0.0001) vs. CTR. No significant differences were observed between CTR and PRO groups in vaginal pH ( p > 0.05). Microbiota analysis based on the 16 S rRNA gene showed no significant differences in differential abundance between CTR and PRO groups at the genus level (q > 0.05). However, PERMANOVA with paired design revealed a significant effect of the group x timepoint model on microbial community composition ( p = 0.004). This is the first study characterizing the vaginal microbiota of cows treated with probiotic LAB strains. Lactobacillus rhamnosus and Lactobacillus reuteri at the tested concentration did not alter vaginal pH up to Day 14 and did not significantly change individual taxon abundances at Days 4 or 7; however, paired analysis detected a significant compositional shift associated with treatment.

Decoupled vegetation structure and composition in a mangrove–apicum ecotone in Northeastern Brazil
abstractText: Abstract Mangrove–apicum ecotones are heterogeneous transition zones in which woody colonization need not follow a single age-ordered trajectory. We reanalysed an author-validated area-level matrix from ten successional mangrove patches in the Barra de Gramame estuary, northeastern Brazil. Five patches belonged to a 6–10-year and five to an 11–15-year site-history category inherited from the original survey. Individuals of Avicennia schaueriana , Laguncularia racemosa and Rhizophora mangle were classified into two height-defined structural strata (< 1 m and >1 m) and counted over 225 m2 per patch; a single 900 m2 reference stand was used descriptively. Hierarchical Bayesian modelling, fully enumerated exact permutations, Bray–Curtis and Aitchison analyses, beta-diversity partitioning and leave-one-area-out diagnostics were applied. The <1 m stratum contained 7,439 individuals, compared with 1,898 individuals in the >1 m stratum. Posterior density ratios (< 1 m/>1 m) were 2.73 (95% credible interval: 1.46–5.12) in 6–10-year areas and 3.64 (1.94–6.73) in 11–15-year areas, whereas site-history effects remained uncertain. Abundance-sensitive assemblage structure differed significantly between height strata (Bray–Curtis R2 = 0.213, exact P = 0.00195), whereas relative species composition did not clearly differ under Aitchison geometry (R2 = 0.029, P = 0.105). Abundance gradients accounted for 96.1% of paired Bray–Curtis dissimilarity, and areas in the older site-history category were not consistently more similar to the reference stand. The ecotone therefore showed a marked height-structure imbalance without equivalent proportional species turnover, while the two coarse site-history categories did not define discrete compositional states. These cross-sectional results support multidimensional, site-specific monitoring and do not by themselves demonstrate a temporal successional trajectory.

Human-made structures as nesting sites for hummingbirds across the Americas: insights from citizen science
abstractText: Abstract Urbanization can negatively affect nesting and reproductive behaviors of birds. Even so, certain species can survive in abundance despite its negative impacts, due to their ability to use alternative human-made structures as nesting sites. There are several studies focusing on hummingbirds’ floral resource use in urban environments, however, little is known about their reproduction and nesting in these areas. Here, we used 5,136 nest photographic records from WikiAves and eBird , two widely used crowdsourcing citizen science platforms, to assess hummingbird nest site choice in natural and anthropized environments across the Americas. We found that 74 hummingbird species (32.03% of the sampled and 20.22% of known species) used diverse human-made substrates as nesting sites or built nests in anthropized environments. This use was observed across almost all clades and its detection was related to sampling effort, but not to species’ body mass, a trait often associated with hummingbird occurrence in urban areas. Overall, these results could indicate behavioral plasticity in some hummingbird species reproductive behavior and nesting resource use, besides their ability to incorporate novel floral resources and nectar feeders in their diet across human-modified areas. Because plants were their preferred nesting sites even in anthropized environments, the importance of maintaining vegetation in transformed and urbanized areas to support these pollinator populations is highlighted. Finally, our results also emphasize the potential of citizen science to provide large amounts of data across extensive geographical regions that would otherwise be difficult to obtain.

The relationship between shooting accuracy and pain perception across different heart rate zones in a youth basketball team
abstractText: Abstract Fatigue can impair shooting accuracy in basketball, but how shooting accuracy and exercise-induced pain change across heart-rate-defined exercise intensities, and how they are related, remains unclear. This study examined free-throw and three-point shooting accuracy and perceived pain across progressively increasing heart-rate zones in youth basketball players. Twelve male basketball players (age 15.50 ± 0.52 years; training experience 4.42 ± 1.44 years) performed a 20-m shuttle run test that was paused at five target zones (Stages 1–5: 50–60% to 90–100% of age-predicted maximum heart rate [HRmax], 220 − age). At each stage, participants rated their pain on a 0–10 numerical pain rating scale and performed five free throws and five three-point shots. Data were analysed with Friedman tests (Kendall’s W), Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with exact p-values and Holm–Bonferroni correction, and Spearman correlations. From Stage 1 to Stage 5, free-throw performance decreased from 3.50 ± 0.52 (70.0%) to 1.67 ± 0.49 (33.3%) successful attempts (χ²(4) = 36.28, p < .001, W = 0.76) and three-point performance from 3.25 ± 0.62 (65.0%) to 0.58 ± 0.67 (11.7%) (χ²(4) = 34.92, p < .001, W = 0.73), whereas pain increased from 1.00 ± 0.74 to 4.92 ± 1.51 (χ²(4) = 47.30, p < .001, W = 0.99). For both shot types, performance in Stage 5 was lower than in all other stages (Holm-adjusted p ≤ .016). Pain was negatively correlated with three-point performance in Stage 4 (ρ = −0.85, Holm-adjusted p = .004); the correlation with free-throw performance in Stage 5 (ρ = −0.63, p = .030) was not significant after correction. In exploratory analyses, training experience was negatively correlated with pain in Stages 2 and 3 (ρ = −0.84, Holm-adjusted p = .012) but was not significantly associated with shooting performance after correction. During a progressive protocol, shooting accuracy declined and pain increased, with the largest decline at the highest stage, and higher pain was associated with lower three-point accuracy at 80–90% of predicted HRmax. Because the stages were performed in a fixed order, the effects of intensity cannot be separated from cumulative fatigue. These findings should be confirmed in larger samples using individually measured HRmax.

title: Pedagogi Kepedulian Dalam Pendidikan Agama Islam: Dialog Kritis Antara Etika Kepedulian Nel Noddings Dan Konsep Rahmah
abstractText: Kepedulian dalam Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) memerlukan penjelasan mengenai hubungan antara niat baik guru, tindakan membimbing, dan pengalaman peserta didik, terutama ketika otoritas pendidikan berhadapan dengan kebutuhan serta keberatan mereka. Artikel ini bertujuan mendialogkan secara kritis etika kepedulian Nel Noddings dan konsep rahmah untuk merumuskan kerangka pertimbangan pedagogis dalam PAI. Kajian menggunakan penelitian kepustakaan dengan pendekatan filosofis-komparatif. Analisis mencakup rekonstruksi argumentasi, klarifikasi konsep, perbandingan kritis, dan perumusan implikasi pedagogis berdasarkan literatur kepedulian serta pembacaan etis-pedagogis QS. Ali ‘Imran [3]:159 yang didukung kajian penafsiran. Analisis menunjukkan bahwa kedua perspektif berjumpa pada perhatian terhadap hubungan dan cara memperlakukan orang lain, tetapi memiliki perbedaan dasar pembenaran moral. Dialog keduanya menghasilkan rumusan bahwa respons peserta didik merupakan sumber pengetahuan untuk mengevaluasi tindakan pendidikan, tanpa menjadi satu-satunya ukuran kelayakan keputusan guru. Otoritas pedagogis perlu dijalankan melalui bimbingan yang menjelaskan tujuan, mempertimbangkan keadaan konkret, menjaga martabat, dan terbuka terhadap koreksi. Sintesis ini menghasilkan lima prinsip: mengenali pribadi peserta didik, menjelaskan tujuan tindakan, menjaga martabat, membuka ruang respons, dan memeriksa kembali keputusan. Kontribusi artikel terletak pada kerangka yang menghubungkan dasar normatif, pelaksanaan tindakan, dan evaluasi hubungan untuk menelaah risiko kepedulian paternalistik dalam PAI. Kerangka ini bersifat konseptual; perluasan telaah tafsir primer dan pengujian empiris diperlukan untuk menilai penerapan serta keterbatasannya.

title: To Test or Not to Test? A Dilemma in Prenatal Testing for an Adult-Onset Genetic Condition
abstractText: Pediatric genetic testing for adult-onset genetic conditions is controversial and generally not recommended because of concerns about protecting a future child’s autonomy to decide as an adult whether to know their genetic status. Yet, preimplantation genetic testing of embryos and prenatal diagnosis of fetuses for adult-onset genetic conditions are routinely offered to at-risk prospective parents when parents intend to select unaffected embryos or terminate an affected pregnancy to avoid having a child with the condition. These commentaries consider a case in which expecting parents (1 of whom is at risk) request prenatal testing for Huntington disease (HD), a genetic, progressive, adult-onset neurological condition, but do not intend to terminate the pregnancy if affected. Such situations highlight the tension between protecting a potential child’s interest in an open future and honoring prospective parents’ reproductive autonomy and ability to make decisions that they determine to be in the best interests of their family and future child. The first commentary highlights ethical distinctions in the case from obstetric and pediatric perspectives. The second commentary considers the role of parental reason-giving in shifting ethical reasoning and deliberation between prenatal and pediatric frames of reference. The third commentary, from the perspective of an HD community member, offers reflections on the breadth of personal and family experiences of HD that may inform choices about prenatal testing. The fourth commentary considers clinicians’ process-related obligations while counseling families about prenatal testing for adult-onset conditions to argue for a shared decision-making model.

title: Design, Implementation, and Empirical Evaluation of a Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model in Higher Education
abstractText: AI-supported assessment increasingly enables adaptive tasks, automated analysis, and personalized feedback, yet their integration into coherent, human-supervised formative assessment remains insufficiently established. This study developed and evaluated the Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model (HA-CAAM) using Design and Development Research structured through the ADDIE framework. Implemented in a higher-education Media Education course, the model employed performance-responsive task adaptation using predefined thresholds, rubric-guided AI-assisted scoring, formative feedback, and instructor verification. Five experts validated the model, 148 students provided quantitative and qualitative implementation feedback, and 50 student responses were independently assessed by two human raters and AI. Expert validation provided initial evidence of content validity (mean Aiken's V = 0.818). Students reported generally favorable experiences, particularly regarding clarity and feedback usefulness, although Learning Support and Overall User Experience received comparatively lower ratings. AI-generated scores demonstrated strong agreement with human-reference scores (ICC = 0.898), despite individual discrepancies. These findings provide initial evidence of content validity, positive implementation experiences, and scoring agreement, rather than demonstrated improvements in learning outcomes or equivalence between AI and human assessment decisions. HA-CAAM contributes an empirically refined, seven-stage assessment framework that coordinates performance-responsive adaptation, AI-assisted analysis, formative feedback, and instructor-led quality assurance within a human-supervised assessment process.

abstractText: ABSTRACT This study was motivated by students’ low proficiency in writing persuasive texts, particularly in developing ideas, constructing arguments, and producing well-organized compositions. It aimed to improve students’ persuasive writing skills through the implementation of the brainwriting technique in Indonesian language learning. The study employed classroom action research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model and was conducted in two cycles. The participants were 32 students from Class VIII-A of SMP Negeri 1 Kalibawang. Data were collected through observations of student engagement and assessments of written texts based on five aspects: content, organization, language, vocabulary, and mechanics. The findings revealed an increase in student engagement from 56.25% in Cycle I to 93.75% in Cycle II. Students’ average writing scores also improved from 61.63 at baseline to 74.91 in Cycle I and 80.50 in Cycle II. Learning mastery increased from 0% at baseline to 53.13% in Cycle I and reached 96.88% in Cycle II. These improvements indicate that the implementation of brainwriting contributed positively to student participation and the development of persuasive writing skills. Therefore, this technique can be adopted as an alternative collaborative learning strategy to support idea generation and improve students’ writing quality. Serum platelet-derived growth factor-BB as a noninvasive biomarker of significant liver fibrosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major cause of progressive liver fibrosis (LF), cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Although noninvasive fibrosis assessment is essential, current tools have practical and diagnostic limitations. Platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)—a profibrogenic mediator of hepatic stellate cell activation—may be a biologically relevant fibrosis biomarker. This study examined the ability of serum PDGF-BB to detect significant fibrosis in CHB patients which is defined as liver stiffness > 7 kPa by vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE; FibroScan). Methods This cross-sectional exploratory diagnostic accuracy study included 90 treatment-naive adults with CHB attending Tanta University Hospitals and Kafr El-Sheikh University Hospitals. All participants underwent clinical evaluation; routine laboratory testing, including HBsAg, HBeAg, and serum HBV DNA; abdominal ultrasonography; serum PDGF-BB measurement by ELISA; and FibroScan examination. VCTE-defined significant fibrosis (F2–F4) was set as liver stiffness > 7 kPa. A non-randomized convenience sampling approach was used to enroll participants, and the optimal PDGF-BB cutoff was established based on the ROC curve derived from this cohort. Results Among 90 patients, 69 (76.7%) had F0-F1 fibrosis and 21 (23.3%) had F2-F4 fibrosis. HBeAg was positive in 21.1% of patients and median HBV DNA was 4.47 (3.68–5.31) log10 IU/mL Median serum PDGF-BB was significantly increased in patients with F2-F4 than in those with F0-F1 fibrosis: 2500.8 (2028.25-2721.8) vs. 777.13 (479.21-1743.15) pg/mL, respectively ( p < 0.001). Serum PDGF-BB discriminated VCTE-defined significant fibrosis at an exploratory, internally derived cutoff of ≥ 1885.9 pg/mL, with an AUC of 0.905 (95% CI 0.816–0.994), sensitivity of 85.7%, specificity of 84.1%, positive predictive value of 62.1%, negative predictive value of 95.1% (at the 23.3% prevalence of this cohort), and overall accuracy of 84.4% (Youden index 0.698; p < 0.001). PDGF-BB had a numerically higher AUC than APRI (0.717) and GPR (0.715), but these differences did not reach statistical significance after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. It did not differ significantly from FIB-4 (0.780) and did not outperform platelet count (0.980) or INR (0.931). Conclusions Serum PDGF-BB demonstrated good discrimination for VCTE-defined significant fibrosis in treatment-naive patients with CHB. Its negative predictive value of 95%, though prevalence-dependent, suggests potential utility as a triage or adjunctive biomarker. However, these findings are preliminary and require external validation before clinical implementation or substitution for elastography.

abstractText: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have changed how undergraduate students approach written coursework, often bypassing required levels of active reading and conceptual engagement. To encourage genuine interaction with course content without resorting to high-stress invigilated exams, a low-stakes digital animation task (2% weighting) was integrated into an undergraduate microbiology and immunology course, to pilot students’ preferences on using animation tools to construct visuals. Students created a 30-s animation, illustrating dynamic biological processes, such as viral replication or phagocytosis. Pre- and post-exercise surveys evaluated students’ prior tool experience, selection criteria and software adoption. Pre-survey results showed that only 57% of students had prior animation experience – predominantly using Microsoft PowerPoint (32%). Key tool selection criteria included user-friendliness (32%), available tutorial support (18%) and zero cost (15%). Following targeted tutorial support for in-house digital tools (e.g. Adobe Express, Adobe Animate, Adobe Character Animator) and autonomy to select Adobe or other preferred tools for the task, post-survey analysis demonstrated a substantial rise in preference for Adobe Express, growing from 2 to 41%, while maintaining high levels of student engagement. Tutors observed that translating biological concepts into moving representations required greater time-on-task, research and deconstruction of study content to construct an accurate visual, thus offering an effective, AI-resistant assessment strategy for science education.

Rational Synthesis of Sulfonic Acid-Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Capture of Trace Strontium in Natural Mineral Water
abstractText: Abstract As a typical long-lived radionuclide, strontium-90 (90Sr) possesses persistent radiological hazards and exhibits high migratory and diffusive behaviors in groundwater. However, the development of adsorbents for the efficient and highly selective capture of trace Sr(II) remains a great challenge. In this study, covalent organic frameworks (COFs, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H) with different numbers of sulfonic acid groups were rationally synthesized and applied for capturing Sr(II). The introduction of sulfonic acid groups onto TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H endowed them with high adsorption capacities of 136.4 and 68.3 mg g–1 toward Sr(II), which were 12-fold and 6-fold higher than that of TpPa without sulfonic acid groups, respectively. Meanwhile, TpPa-2SO3H and TpPa-SO3H exhibited fast adsorption kinetics, capturing 99% of Sr(II) within 3 and 10 min, respectively. In addition, TpPa-2SO3H also exhibited high selectivity, excellent anti-interference performance, and regeneration ability without high calcium backgrounds. Characterizations and theoretical calculations demonstrated that sulfonic acid groups in TpPa-2SO3H promoted Sr(II) capture through strong ion-exchange interaction. TpPa-2SO3H was further applied to extract trace Sr(II) in natural Sr-containing mineral water samples. The results showed that the extraction efficiency for Sr(II) exceeded 95% within 5 min. Furthermore, the selectivity for Sr(II) was investigated by the distribution coefficients (Kd), and the Kd was 5.6 × 104 mL g–1 for TpPa-2SO3H toward Sr(II), approximately 400 times higher than those of Na(I) and K(I), respectively. This work not only developed a promising strategy to extract trace Sr(II) from real samples but also broadened the application of COFs in separation science.

title: Islamic family law perspective on livelihood provision by visually impaired husbands: A study at the Indonesian Moslem Blind Association (ITMI) Manado
abstractText: Purpose – This study aims to analyze the fulfillment of family support obligations by visually impaired husbands in the Indonesian Muslim Blind Association (ITMI) in Manado City, using the perspective of Islamic family law. Design – This study uses a qualitative method with a case study approach. Primary data was obtained by conducting in-depth interviews with husbands of visually impaired individuals as well as ITMI administrators. Secondary data was based on Law No. 1 of 1974 concerning marriage, from books and journals, using analysis techniques through data reduction, presentation, and drawing conclusions. Findings – Research results show that even though they have physical limitations, blind husbands at ITMI still try their best to meet their family's economic needs through various professions (like massage therapists, farmers, traditional healers). In situations where the economic needs aren't fully met, there's cooperation and compromise in the family, with the wives also pitching in financially. Research Implications – This research provides a theoretical contribution to the development of inclusive Islamic family law studies based on humanity (equality and decency). Practically, this research is expected to serve as a reference for local governments and social institutions in formulating economic empowerment policies and accessibility assistance for people with disabilities. Originality – The novelty of this research lies in its focus, which connects Islamic family law with the sociological realities of visually impaired people in urban areas of Manado city, something that hasn't been explored in depth very often.

title: Medicaid Value-Based Payment and Quality of Serious Mental Illness Care: Does the Association Vary Across Racial and Ethnic Groups?
abstractText: Abstract While there is growing interest in the implementation of value-based payment (VBP) policies in Medicaid, there is little evidence on whether their impacts among high-need beneficiaries vary by race and ethnicity. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Oregon Medicaid data and a pre-experimental, treatment-only repeated cross-sectional panel design, to examine whether the association of Oregon’s Medicaid VBP policy with quality varied by race and ethnicity among the state’s beneficiaries with serious mental illness (SMI), that is, those diagnosed with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or severe major depressive disorder. We estimated changes in 12 quality measures, by race and ethnicity, pre (2010–2012) and post (2013–2019) VBP implementation. Seven of the 12 measures were designated as VBP performance metrics, with Follow-up after Hospitalization for Mental Illness, 7-day (FUH-7-day), also designated as a bonus-earning incentive metric. The cohort totaled 232,791 person-years (71,599 beneficiaries), with 89% self-described as White and the balance as Latinamerican or Black. The policy was associated with improved quality on FUH-7-day and FUH-30-day, and decreased quality on three physical healthcare measures. The quality impacts varied by race and ethnicity. The policy was associated with the elimination of a pre-existing schizophrenia-only Latinamerican-White FUH-7-day disparity due to the relatively larger Latinamerican post-VBP increase of 18.4 percentage points (95% CI, 2.2–34.6). However, the minority-White disparities in the Antidepressant Medication Management measures persisted post-VBP, and pre-existing advantages for Latinamerican beneficiaries in Cervical Cancer Screening and Avoidance of All-Cause Readmission disappeared because Latinamerican beneficiaries’ performance worsened post-VBP. This study of Oregon’s mature VBP policy contributes first evidence of the potential impacts of Medicaid VBP policies on quality disparities among beneficiaries with SMI. Findings suggest modest gains, potentially related to targeted financial incentives, while also revealing a potential for stagnant or worsening performance.

title: Energy transfer in shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interactions
abstractText: Abstract The energy transport and exchange processes among the mean kinetic energy (MKE), turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), mean internal energy and turbulent internal energy in a shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interaction (SBLI) are quantified using direct numerical simulations. By analyzing the transport budgets of mean and fluctuating energy modes, the primary mechanisms governing energy transfer cycles within the interaction region are identified. Results show that energy transfer is dominated by three key processes: turbulence production ( $$P_k$$ P k ), which transfers energy from the mean flow to turbulence, mean pressure dilatation ( $$\Phi^{pm}$$ Φ pm ), which mediates the compressibility-driven energy exchange between MKE and mean internal energy, and viscous dissipation ( $$\varepsilon$$ ε ), which irreversibly converts TKE into mean internal energy. The effects of variable density and terms related to turbulent internal energy are found to be negligible. The present work clarifies the essential energy transfer pathways in SBLI, offering valuable insights for the development of improved turbulence closure models and the design of effective flow control strategies.

The centriole as a fourth counter of replicative aging: a systems analysis of ARGUS, an open autonomous platform for lineage-scale surveillance
abstractText: Replicative aging in dividing cells is commonly described through three resettable counters: telomere length, mitochondrial state, and chromatin organisation. We argue for a fourth: the centriole, a conserved microtubule-based organelle that every animal cell either keeps or eliminates. Three lines of evidence motivate the proposal. First, centriole fate is highly stereotyped: in Caenorhabditis elegans about 88% of somatic cells eliminate their centrioles during embryogenesis, and elimination is coupled to cell fate (Kalbfuss & Gönczy, 2023a). Second, centriole age measurably biases division geometry and cell fate in human cells, including asymmetric inheritance in stem cells (Thomas & Meraldi, 2024; Izumi et al., 2026). Third, unlike telomeres, mitochondria, and chromatin, the centriole has no known disposal-and-reassembly pathway in somatic cells, yet nature performs an analogous reset between meiosis I and the first blastomeres, at the cost of haploidization (Pierron et al., 2023). We present a systems analysis of ARGUS, an open, autonomous, low-cost fluorescence platform for lineage-scale surveillance of centrioles in living specimens, and of its four operating subsystems (OS1–OS4). The subsystems form an epistemic ladder. OS1 asks whether division geometry, summarised as a pre-registered Pedigree Score, predicts centriole fate (correlation). OS2 asks whether pedigree predicts convergence of fate across different lineages (prediction). OS3 tests causality through laser ablation (necessity) and centriole transplantation (sufficiency), and asks whether centriole elimination followed by de novo synthesis can reset cellular entropy without haploidization. OS4 adds inverted-geometry high-numerical-aperture imaging and contact-free optoelectronic-tweezer manipulation. Each stage carries pre-registered, falsifiable criteria and explicit go/no-go gates. We analyse the epistemic structure of the system, its failure modes, and its generalisability, and discuss what a testable fourth counter implies for aging biology and for open, autonomous biological instrumentation.

title: Quaternary Coding Theory of the Biological Ledger over GF(4): Evaluation Codes, Plaquette Checks, and Conditional Syndrome Decoding
abstractText: We construct explicit quaternary error-correcting codes for abstract locus, contact and lattice registers motivated by the Chrysene Formalism. Evaluation on the four affine points of $\mathrm{GF}(4)$ gives the Euclidean self-dual MDS code $[4,2,3]_4$. The five projective points give the perfect Hamming code $[5,3,3]_4$, whose 64 radius-one spheres partition $\mathrm{GF}(4)^5$; their tensor product is a $[20,6,9]_4$ array code correcting four arbitrary symbol errors. On the cubical box $B(3,3,6)$, the cycle and cut codes have parameters $[117,64,4]_4$ and $[117,53,3]_4$. Their full CSS check pair commutes and has zero logical dimension. An ideal 16-outcome syndrome instrument preserves each syndrome subspace and enables exact classical single-symbol correction. For independent symbol errors of probability $p$, decoded block failure is $10p^2-20p^3+15p^4-4p^5$. We compare uncoded blocks at both fixed coordinate count and equal information payload, distinguish binary-logistic and four-level Gibbs calibrations, and compute their conditional splitting thresholds. At complete quaternary randomization, $p=3/4$, channel capacity is zero and decoder success is only $1/64$. Molecular encoders, Berry-phase readout and Stark control are explicit realization targets rather than consequences of code cardinalities. Executable finite verification and a scoped Lean companion accompany the constructions.

Circulating metabolic subtypes and proteomic signatures associated with incident idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a UK biobank prospective cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is biologically heterogeneous, but whether circulating metabolic/biomarker heterogeneity and complementary proteomic information can prospectively identify individuals at different risks of incident IPF and improve risk prediction remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 9,443 UK Biobank participants with 308 baseline metabolic/biomarker (Met/Bio) traits and 2,909 plasma proteins. Participants were separated into training, internal validation, and geographically separated external validation sets before imputation and feature selection. Training-set LASSO selection, principal component analysis, and K-means clustering were used to derive Met/Bio subtypes. Incident IPF risk was assessed across subtypes. Within the highest-burden subtype, protein-wide associations were evaluated using complementary Cox approaches, and random-forest models integrating conventional factors, Met/Bio traits, and proteins were assessed at 5, 10, and 15 years. Results During 128,534 person-years of follow-up, 90 incident IPF cases occurred. Twenty-seven Met/Bio traits defined three reproducible subtypes. C3, characterized by a triglyceride-rich VLDL profile together with inflammatory features, had the highest observed IPF burden, with the overall risk pattern reproduced in both validation sets. Within C3, five proteins—CD80, ADA2, CDCP1, CCL7, and DPEP1—showed robust associations with incident IPF across unpenalized, ridge, and Firth Cox analyses. Compared with the Basic model, the integrated Basic+Met/Bio+Pro model increased 5-, 10-, and 15-year AUCs from 0.573, 0.659, and 0.705 to 0.851, 0.725, and 0.757 in internal validation and from 0.891, 0.650, and 0.692 to 0.971, 0.939, and 0.808 in geographically separated external validation. Conclusions Circulating Met/Bio subtyping identified reproducible heterogeneity in incident IPF risk and a risk-enriched subtype. Integrating Met/Bio and proteomic information showed proof-of-concept predictive improvement beyond conventional factors, warranting validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: Bidentate Chelation-Driven Selective Depression of Pyrite: Adsorption Mechanism and Flotation Application of an N-Heterocyclic Carboxylic Acid Depressant
abstractText: Abstract The selective flotation separation of chalcopyrite and pyrite constitutes a core bottleneck in the comprehensive utilization of copper–sulfur ores. Given the proneness of pyrite to copper activation and pipeline scaling defects induced by the conventional high-alkaline lime depression process, novel organic depressants with outstanding selectivity under weak alkaline media are urgently required to be developed. In this study, 3-hydroxy-2-pyridine carboxylic acid (3-HPA) was adopted as a novel eco-friendly organic depressant to realize the selective flotation separation of chalcopyrite from pyrite under weakly acidic conditions (pH = 6). The selective depression mechanism of 3-HPA against pyrite was systematically investigated via microflotation assays, multiscale surface characterizations, and first-principles theoretical computations. Flotation experimental data verified that 3-HPA is capable of selectively depressing pyrite floatability while maintaining excellent floatability of chalcopyrite, with a maximum recovery gap of 92.71% observed between the two minerals. Collectively, 3-HPA serves as an efficient and highly selective organic depressant for pyrite. On pyrite surfaces, 3-HPA undergoes bidentate chelation with surface iron active sites: the nitrogen atom on its pyridine ring and the oxygen atoms of the carboxyl group coordinate with Fe atoms to generate stable Fe–N and Fe–O bonds, which drastically reduce the surface hydrophobicity of pyrite. By comparison, only feeble intermolecular interactions take place between 3-HPA and chalcopyrite surfaces, whereby the surface hydrophobicity of chalcopyrite remains intact. The present research clarifies the selective depression mechanism of 3-HPA against pyrite and provides new theoretical guidance for the development of green and efficient pyrite depressants.

title: Proton conducting Cicer arietinum L starch electrolyte doped with NH4SCN for electrochemical double layer capacitors
abstractText: Abstract A chickpea starch–agar biopolymer electrolyte plasticized with glycerol and doped with NH 4 SCN was successfully developed for symmetric electrochemical double-layer capacitor (EDLC) applications. FTIR confirmed the interaction between NH 4 SCN and the biopolymer matrix, while XRD revealed increasing amorphous character with salt addition. The optimized CSA5 electrolyte exhibited a maximum ionic conductivity of 1.1 × 10 − 3 S cm −1 , a low bulk resistance of 43.60 Ω, an ionic transference number of 0.89, an electrochemical stability window of 1.8 V, and good thermal stability. The EDLC exhibited a specific capacitance of 40.0 F g −1 at 5 mV s −1 from CV, decreasing to 3.9 F g −1 at 70 mV s −1 . From GCD measurements, the specific capacitance decreased from 42.14 F g −1 at 0.15 mA to 21.28 F g −1 at 0.25 mA. The corresponding energy density decreased from 5.85 to 2.95 Wh kg −1 , while the power density increased from approximately 375–625 W kg −1 . The rate-dependent capacitance indicates limitations in ion transport and electrode/electrolyte interfacial accessibility at higher scan and current rates. Overall, the CSA5 electrolyte demonstrates the basic electrochemical functionality required for solid-state EDLC applications and provides a preliminary assessment of its energy-storage potential.

title: The Effect of ChatGPT Use on Students’ Reflection on Pancasila and Citizenship Education Learning Materials
abstractText: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) into education has created new opportunities to support reflective learning; however, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between ChatGPT use and learning reflection in Pancasila and Citizenship Education remains limited. This study examined the relationship between ChatGPT use and students' learning reflection among Grade XI students. A quantitative correlational design was employed involving 56 Grade XI students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using validated questionnaires comprising 15 items measuring ChatGPT Use and 12 items measuring Learning Reflection. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression. The results demonstrated a positive and statistically significant relationship between ChatGPT use and learning reflection (R² = 0.813, p < 0.001). Descriptive analysis indicated that ChatGPT Use (M = 54.21, SD = 3.57) and learning reflection (M = 42.77, SD = 4.38) were classified as being in the "Good" category. These findings suggest that ChatGPT can support reflective learning when integrated into well-designed pedagogical activities under teacher guidance. This study contributes empirical evidence regarding the educational use of Generative AI in Pancasila and Citizenship Education and provides practical implications for promoting reflective and responsible learning.

title: Zeolite-Confined Triatomic Cu Oxides at Silanol Nests as Hydrogen Transport Channels for H2 Production from Methanol Steam Reforming
abstractText: Abstract Cu-based catalysts offer high methanol steam reforming (MSR) activity but are limited by unstable Cu+–Cu0 interconversions due to the redox and sintering labilities of Cu. Herein, we developed a universal amino-functionalized “gripper” strategy for firmly and precisely anchoring atomically dispersed metals (e.g., Cu, Co, Ni) within Beta-zeolite. Triatomic Cu oxide (Cu3Ox) sites lower the methanol dehydrogenation activation barrier, and the synergistic interplay with adjacent OH groups from silanol nests accelerates H2 evolution and the MSR reaction. Spatially decoupling Cu-mediated methanol activation from silanol-driven H2 evolution at silanol nests as proton transport channels within the confining zeolite framework also effectively protected Cu from sintering, achieving a high specific activity of 951 molH2·molCu–1·h–1 and over 600 h of stability under continuous regeneration. This work provides a universal strategy for synthesizing atomically dispersed metal catalysts and a new design principle for maintaining the Cu structure during MSR.

Developing a Workplace Mental-Health Profiling Database System Integrated with Islamic Values
abstractText: Workplace mental-health profiling systems promise early intervention and psychosocial risk mitigation, yet in employment settings they introduce acute hazards of managerial surveillance, coercion, discrimination, and moral misclassification. This article develops a conceptual model for workplace mental-health profiling within Muslim-majority contexts by integrating Islamic ethical principles with Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory and privacy-by-design governance. It contends that Islamic ethics must function not as ornamental religious rhetoric, but as an institutional constraint on corporate power. Foundational concepts—specifically tawḥīd (divine unity), fiṭrah (primordial nature), iḥsān (moral excellence), amānah (fiduciary trust), sirr (confidentiality), and ʿadl (justice)—reorient profiling from individual risk categorisation toward structural psychosocial risk governance, employee dignity, confidentiality, and institutional accountability. Applying design-science conceptual modelling, this normative framework is operationalised into explicit system parameters: voluntary participation, enforceable non-retaliation guarantees, strict data minimisation, complete insulation from performance appraisals, aggregate-only reporting, and the absolute prohibition of spiritual data extraction.

title: Intra-articular knee injections in adults aged 40 to 60 years and the likelihood of progression to joint arthroplasty
abstractText: Aims Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a common cause of pain and disability in adults. Intra-articular injections are important components in the management of knee OA symptoms, but there are concerns that these injections may be associated with the progression of OA. Therefore, this study determined how the likelihood of progression to arthroplasty is influenced by intra-articular injection of corticosteroid (CS) and/or hyaluronic acid (HA) in patients with knee OA. Methods This population-based cohort study included patients aged 40 to 60 years receiving an initial intra-articular injection of CS and/or HA from 1 January 2000 through 31 December 2010, who resided in Olmsted County, Minnesota, USA. The primary outcome was the likelihood of joint arthroplasty by number of intra-articular injections received evaluated by Cox proportional hazards regression. Results A total of 1,897 patients (n = 2,336 knees) who received 8,600 injections (n = 5,786 CS; n = 2,814 HA) were included (mean age 51.9 years (SD 5.5); 1,515 females (64.9%); mean BMI 34.8 kg/m 2 (SD 8.0)), and 917 (39.3%) subsequently underwent arthroplasty. Accounting for age, BMI, and Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grade at initial injection, the number of intra-articular injections was associated with an increased likelihood of arthroplasty (hazard ratio (HR) 1.12 (95% CI 1.08 to 1.17)). For patients with early OA (KL grade 0 to 1), CS injections (HR 1.27 (95% CI 1.17 to 1.37)) were associated with an increased likelihood of arthroplasty versus HA (HR 1.12 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.19)). Conclusion Each intra-articular injection was associated with a 12% increased likelihood of arthroplasty. With subgroup analysis, CS injections in early OA were associated with a 27% increased likelihood of arthroplasty. Cite this article: Bone Jt Open 2026;7(11):1462–1470.

title: SISTEM MONITORING LEVEL AIR DAN PENGENDALIAN POMPA OTOMATIS BERBASIS SENSOR ULTRASONIK AO2YY4W DAN ESP32
abstractText: Manual filling of water tanks may cause overflow and unnecessary electricity consumption when the pump continues to operate after the tank reaches its maximum level. This study aims to develop an automatic water level monitoring and pump control system using an A02YY4W RS485 ultrasonic sensor and an ESP32. An experimental method with a prototype approach was employed. The system uses the A02YY4W ultrasonic sensor to measure water level, an LM35 to monitor water temperature, an ESP32 as the processing and control unit, an RS485 to TTL module as the communication interface, and a relay to control the water pump. System information is displayed through a local web server hosted on the ESP32. Sensor calibration was conducted at 10 water-level variations, resulting in an average absolute difference of 0.60 cm and an average error of 1.86%. Filling tests were performed from initial water levels of 0%, 25%, and 50% until reaching the maximum level of 100%. The results show that the system can track water-level changes and control the pump automatically. Fluctuations were mainly observed during filling from lower initial levels due to water surface movement, but they did not interfere with the control function. Changes in water level, temperature, and pump status were displayed through the web interface. The developed system is suitable for automatic water level monitoring and pump control in water storage systems.

title: Efficacy of prolonged adjuvant imatinib in gastrointestinal stromal tumors: a systematic review and exploratory network meta-analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Three years of adjuvant imatinib is the established standard for patients with high-risk gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), but recurrence after treatment cessation raises questions about longer treatment durations. This study evaluated evidence on extended adjuvant therapy, emphasizing treatment beyond 3 years and factors relevant to patient selection. Methods PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through April 19, 2026. Randomized controlled trials, prospective single-arm studies, and cohort studies were included in the systematic review. An exploratory frequentist network meta-analysis (NMA) compared recurrence-related survival outcomes across placebo/observation and 1-, 3-, and 6-year adjuvant imatinib strategies. Results Twenty-two reports representing 13 independent studies (four randomized trials, two prospective single-arm trials, and seven cohort studies) were included. IMADGIST demonstrated improved DFS with 6 versus 3 years of imatinib (hazard ratio [HR], 0.40; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20–0.69; P = 0.0008). In the three-trial NMA, the 6-year strategy had the highest P-score (0.9994), with an indirect estimated HR of 0.09 (95% CI, 0.04–0.21) versus placebo/observation. However, the linear network, differences in trial populations, and distinct randomization time points limited the interpretation of indirect rankings. While 3 versus 1 year of imatinib demonstrated a long-term overall survival (OS) benefit, an additional OS benefit from treatment beyond 3 years has not been established. Molecular characteristics, recurrence risk, and tolerability were relevant to individualized treatment decisions; in PERSIST-5, 51% completed the planned 5-year course. Conclusions Extending adjuvant imatinib beyond 3 years improves recurrence-related outcomes in selected high-risk GIST patients, but the optimal duration and long-term OS effects remain uncertain. The proposed Personalized Triangle Framework integrates molecular sensitivity, recurrence risk, and tolerability as a conceptual aid rather than a validated treatment-selection algorithm. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

title: Small intestine-restricted Th17 enrichment in TSNO mice is associated with increased SFB colonization and ileal epithelial activation
abstractText: Abstract Background T helper 17 (Th17) cells are highly enriched in the small intestine and play a critical role in mucosal immunity. Their differentiation is strongly influenced by the gut microbiota, particularly segmented filamentous bacteria (SFB), which induce Th17 responses through interactions with intestinal epithelial cells. In parallel, group 3 innate lymphoid cells (ILC3s) contribute to intestinal immune homeostasis via IL-22-mediated epithelial activation. However, how host genetic background regulates the balance between Th17 cells and ILC3s contributes to region-specific Th17 enrichment remains unclear. Methods We quantified immune cell populations, including Th17 cells, regulatory T cells, and ILC3s, in the small intestinal lamina propria of Tsumura Suzuki nonobese (TSNO), Tsumura Suzuki obese diabetes (TSOD), ddY, and C57BL/6 mice using flow cytometry. SFB abundance was quantified using PCR. Ileal epithelial responses were assessed using immunoblotting and gene expression analyses. To determine microbiota dependence, mice were treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) was performed with germ-free C57BL/6 mice as recipients. Reciprocal TSNO × TSOD F1 progeny were analyzed to assess the contribution of host strain background. Results TSNO mice exhibited markedly greater Th17 cell enrichment in the small intestine than TSOD, ddY, and C57BL/6 mice. Conversely, ILC3 frequency in TSNO mice was reduced, indicating that Th17 dominance does not reflect generalized RORγt + lymphoid population expansion. TSNO mice displayed significantly increased ileal colonization by SFB, accompanied by enhanced epithelial responses, characterized by increased STAT3 phosphorylation and antimicrobial and immune-related gene upregulation. Antibiotic treatment reduced SFB abundance and suppressed Th17-associated gene expression, supporting an association between SFB colonization and the intestinal Th17-associated program. FMT showed that microbiota from TSNO and TSOD mice promoted Th17 responses in germ-free recipients, although the TSNO phenotype was not completely reproduced. Reciprocal TSNO × TSOD F1 progeny exhibited intermediate Th17 cell proportions, supporting an association between host genetic background and the observed phenotype. Conclusions TSNO mice represent a unique model of small intestine-restricted Th17 enrichment associated with increased SFB colonization, enhanced epithelial responsiveness, and strain-associated host factors. Increased SFB colonization may contribute to the early establishment of the Th17-enriched state, whereas host and epithelial factors may contribute to its persistence at later ages.

title: Electrochemical [4+1] Annulation of N -(Arylsulfonyl)acrylamides with 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds via Multiple C–H Functionalization
abstractText: Abstract A general electrochemical intermolecular cascade annulation between N-arylacrylamides and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds through C(sp3)–H/C(sp2)–H functionalization and 1,4-aryl migration has been developed. This protocol employs 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds as C1 synthons that undergo [4+1] carboannulation, delivering diverse functionalized indanes with two distinct quaternary carbon centers under noble-metal- and external-oxidant-free conditions. Control experiments indicate that the reaction proceeds via a sequential cascade of oxidative C(sp3)–H cleavage to generate an alkyl radical, radical addition across the C═C bond, 1,4-aryl migration, a further oxidative C(sp3)–H cleavage to form another alkyl radical, [4+1] annulation, and deprotonation.

title: Engineered interface in sunlight-driven non-oxidative ethane dehydrogenation
abstractText: Abstract Photocatalytic reactions powered by solar energy are essential for capitalizing on renewable solar resources. However, efficiently utilizing the entire sunlight spectrum for reactions with high activation energy, such as alkane dehydrogenation, poses a major challenge in catalyst design. In this research, we propose a surface modification strategy that generates abundant interfacial sites on the TiN surface while preserving strong light absorption, promoting interfacial electron-hole recombination, and supporting catalytic reactions across the full spectrum. Through a combination of spectroscopic, theoretical, and experimental investigations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of this catalyst design in enhancing solar energy utilization. We have successfully developed a SrTiO3/SrOx-TiN catalyst that significantly enhances the activity of non-oxidative ethane dehydrogenation by 11.7-fold under solar photocatalysis. The strategy revealed in this work, which involves constructing abundant reaction sites with enhanced interfacial electron-hole recombination, is vital for developing advanced heterogeneous solar photocatalytic systems.

title: Evaluasi Kapasitas dan Efisiensi Ruang Parkir di FMIPA Universitas Negeri Padang
abstractText: Kebutuhan parkir di kawasan perguruan tinggi perlu dinilai berdasarkan jumlah ruang yang tersedia pada suatu waktu dan kemampuan petak melayani kendaraan secara bergantian selama periode operasional. Penelitian ini mengevaluasi kapasitas dan karakteristik parkir sepeda motor serta mobil di Fakultas Matematika dan Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam, Universitas Negeri Padang (FMIPA UNP). Penelitian menggunakan survei observasional kuantitatif-deskriptif: pengamatan pendahuluan pada 9 Maret 2026 dan pencatatan kendaraan masuk-keluar pada 8, 10, dan 12 Juni 2026, masing-masing selama 12 jam. Inventarisasi mencatat 257 satuan ruang parkir (SRP) sepeda motor dan 52 SRP mobil. Pada pengamatan pendahuluan, tercatat 286 sepeda motor dan 55 mobil di area parkir, setara dengan 111,3% dan 105,8% dari kapasitas statis masing-masing jenis. Survei utama menghasilkan volume total 480, 469, dan 439 kendaraan per hari, serta akumulasi maksimum gabungan 192, 189, dan 171 kendaraan. Tingkat pergantian sepeda motor berkisar 1,50–1,66 kendaraan/SRP selama pengamatan, sedangkan mobil sekitar 1,04. Estimasi kapasitas layanan teoritis yang dilaporkan melampaui volume harian; namun nilai tersebut didasarkan pada rata-rata durasi dan bukan pengukuran ketersediaan petak pada setiap saat. Temuan menunjukkan perlunya membedakan indikasi tekanan okupansi sesaat pada pengamatan awal dari potensi layanan harian pada hari survei yang berbeda. Akumulasi maksimum belum dilaporkan terpisah menurut jenis dan zona sehingga frekuensi serta lokasi kejenuhan belum dapat dipastikan. Audit okupansi per jenis/zona, penataan marka, dan pengendalian sirkulasi direkomendasikan sebagai langkah evaluasi lanjutan sebelum memutuskan ekspansi fisik. Parking adequacy on university campuses must be assessed in terms of both the number of spaces available at a given time and their potential daily service through vehicle turnover. This study evaluated motorcycle and car parking characteristics and capacity at the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, Universitas Negeri Padang (FMIPA UNP). A quantitative descriptive observational design included a preliminary observation on March 9, 2026, and entry–exit surveys on June 8, 10, and 12, 2026, conducted for 12 hours each day. The inventory identified 257 motorcycle parking space units and 52 car spaces. The preliminary observation recorded 286 motorcycles and 55 cars on site, corresponding to 111.3% and 105.8% of their respective static space counts. During the main survey, daily combined volumes were 480, 469, and 439 vehicles, while combined peak accumulations were 192, 189, and 171. Motorcycle turnover ranged from 1.50 to 1.66 vehicles per space during the observation period, compared with approximately 1.04 for cars. Reported theoretical service capacities exceeded daily volumes; however, these estimates depend on average parking duration and do not verify space availability throughout the day. The findings highlight the distinction between the preliminary indication of momentary occupancy pressure and theoretical service capacity observed on different dates. Because peak accumulation was not reported separately by vehicle type or parking zone, the frequency and location of saturation remain uncertain. Zone- and vehicle-specific occupancy audits, clearer markings, and circulation management should precede decisions on physical expansion.

title: Rancang Bangun Website Pemesanan Online dan Stock Barang Menggunakan Metode Waterfall di Rumah Makan Minang Ampek Pangeran
abstractText: The current advancement of information technology encourages many culinary business owners to adopt web-based systems. This strategic step is taken to enhance service effectiveness and streamline overall business management. Unfortunately, Rumah Makan Minang Ampek Pangeran still relies on conventional methods for its daily operations. Orders are received through walk-ins or text messages, while food stock is recorded manually in notebooks. This practice frequently causes operational issues, such as susceptibility to recording errors, slow information flow, and difficulty in monitoring food availability. Therefore, this study aims to design and develop an online ordering website integrated with a stock management system. The system development adopts the Waterfall method, encompassing requirement analysis, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance. Data was collected through direct observation and in-depth interviews with the owner and staff. The main features of the website include online ordering services, menu management, customer databases, and food stock management. Testing results demonstrate that this website successfully facilitates customers in placing orders and significantly assists the management. The management can now monitor menu availability more neatly, accurately, and systematically, resulting in vastly improved service efficiency. This system also reduces the risk of recording errors typically found in manual processes. In conclusion, the implementation of this online ordering and stock management system is highly feasible to support the daily operations of the restaurant.

Microbial Bioprocessing of Plant-Based Food Matrices: From Conventional Analysis to In Situ Characterization of Cell Wall-Bound Phenolic Release
abstractText: Abstract The release mechanisms of bound phenolics (BPs) from plant cell walls during bioprocessing, such as microbial fermentation, are highly dynamic and exhibit microscopic spatial selectivity. While conventional chemical analysis can provide macroscopic data on BPs release, it fails to reveal the microscopic spatial heterogeneity and causal relationships underlying the cell wall degradation process. This review examines both conventional extraction-based analytical methods and emerging in situ imaging technologies, such as Raman/FTIR spectroscopy, confocal laser scanning microscopy, immunofluorescence, and mass spectrometry imaging, highlighting their complementary roles and current technical bottlenecks in characterizing BPs release and cell wall degradation. Furthermore, a unified multiscale, multimodal framework is proposed, integrating high-resolution imaging, dynamic fluorescence probes, multidimensional spectroscopy, and machine-learning-assisted data fusion. This holistic characterization strategy elucidates the precise mechanisms governing phenolic release, providing a theoretical basis to guide the targeted enrichment of BPs and advance the efficient utilization of plant biomass and agricultural residues.

Association of Low Birth Weight with Bone Mineral Density and Fracture Occurrence in Postmenopausal Women
abstractText: Abstract Low birth weight (LBW) has been associated with impaired skeletal development and low peak bone mass. However, the association between LBW and fracture risk in postmenopausal women remains un-clear. We analyzed prospectively collected data from the population-based Osteoporosis Risk Factor and Pre-vention (OSTPRE) cohort, including women aged >50 years. Birth weight was categorized as LBW (<2500 g) or normal birth weight (≥2500 g). Fracture outcomes were analyzed using standardized inci-dence ratios (SIRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bone mineral density (BMD) trajectories were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. There were 635 women in the LBW group and 9387 in the normal birth weight group. During follow-up, a total of 8453 fractures occurred. Women with LBW had an 18% higher risk of vertebral fractures (SIR 1.18, 95% CI 1.01–1.39), a 20% higher risk of vertebral or hip fractures combined (SIR 1.20, 95% CI 1.06–1.38), and an 11% higher risk of any osteoporotic fracture (SIR 1.11, 95% CI 1.01–1.22) compared with women with normal birth weight. Hip fracture risk was borderline increased (SIR 1.25, 95% CI 0.99–1.59). No significant differences in BMD levels or age-related BMD decline were observed between the groups. LBW was associated with increased fracture risk in postmenopausal women despite similar BMD trajecto-ries. These findings suggest that adverse early-life conditions may have long-term effects on skeletal fra-gility independent of later-life BMD.

title: Isomeric-Level Description of Complex Bio-Oils Enabled by Gated TIMS Coupled to 18-T FTICR MS
abstractText: Abstract Lignocellulosic biomass is a key renewable resource to produce biofuels via thermochemical processes such as fast pyrolysis and hydrothermal liquefaction. However, the resulting bio-oils are highly complex mixtures containing large numbers of oxygen-containing compounds, making their chemical characterization particularly challenging. While standalone Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FTICR MS) enables ultrahigh-accuracy molecular formula assignment, direct mass spectrometry analysis does not allow isomeric discrimination. This can be overcome by the use of an upfront separation technique such as ion mobility (IM) that separates ions as a function of their size and shape. In this work, a gated trapped ion mobility spectrometry–FTICR MS (gTIMS-FTICR MS) was used for the characterization of bio-oils. First, a mixture of 13 representative standards was analyzed, affording mobility trends for major bio-oil compound families, including carbohydrates, polyphenols, and fatty acids. The method was then applied to three pine-derived bio-oils produced by fast pyrolysis, stabilized fast pyrolysis, and hydrothermal liquefaction. Extracted ion mobilograms (EIMs) revealed extensive isomeric diversity and distinct ion mobility profiles depending on the production and stabilization processes. Descriptors derived from ion mobility distributions, such as the number of fitted Gaussians, apex component 1/K0, and the number of local maxima, provided insights into differences in molecular shape and structural diversity. Overall, gTIMS-FTICR MS proves to be a powerful multidimensional approach for resolving isomeric complexity in bio-oils and for assessing the impact of thermochemical conversion and upgrading processes.

Defect-Tolerant Conduction Band Formation in SrBi3O4Cl3 through Interlayer Bi 6p Orbital Coupling
abstractText: Abstract The control of defect-induced electron trap levels is crucial for regulating the reactivity of photogenerated charge carriers. Although electron trapping can suppress rapid electron–hole recombination, excessive deep trapping lowers the energy and mobility of photogenerated electrons, thereby reducing their reactivity. Thus, controlling trap depth is essential for improving photocatalysts and other photofunctional materials. However, rational design principles remain limited. Here, we compare two layered bismuth oxychlorides, SrBiO2Cl and SrBi3O4Cl3, using time-resolved absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. These materials consist of stacked fluorite-like oxide slabs separated by chloride layers: SrBiO2Cl contains [SrBiO2]+ slabs, whereas SrBi3O4Cl3 contains Bi-rich regions in adjacent slabs that face each other across a single chloride layer. This structural contrast provides a suitable platform to examine how interlayer Bi 6p coupling modifies the conduction band minimum (CBM) and affects defect-induced electron trapping. Transient absorption measurements revealed that photogenerated electrons in SrBiO2Cl are predominantly trapped in deep defect states, whereas SrBi3O4Cl3 retains a substantial population of free and/or shallowly trapped electrons in the microsecond time region. DFT calculations indicated that, in SrBiO2Cl, the absence of effective interlayer Bi–Bi coupling results in a CBM composed of relatively isolated Bi 6p states. In this electronic structure, intrinsic defects, particularly anion vacancies, can create Bi 6p-derived dangling-bond-like states that are further stabilized by local relaxation and rehybridization, forming deep electron traps below the CBM. In contrast, SrBi3O4Cl3 forms an energetically stabilized and spatially extended bonding-type Bi 6p-derived CBM through interlayer Bi–Bi coupling across the single chloride layer. Because this bonding-type CBM is already lowered by interlayer Bi–Bi orbital interactions, defect-derived Bi 6p states do not become deeply separated from the conduction band edge even after local relaxation and rehybridization. As a result, intrinsic bulk deep-trap formation is suppressed. This mechanism provides a design principle for defect-tolerant layered bismuth oxychloride photocatalysts.

title: Al3+ exclusion in macaúba palm diaspores: structural and cytological aspects
abstractText: Abstract The oil palm macaúba ( Acrocomia aculeata ) maintains seed banks in soils rich in Al 3+ of the Cerrado biome. However, the interaction of this cation with complex diaspores such as those of Arecaceae is still poorly understood. We aimed to evaluate the role of diaspore structure and embryonic cytology in the tolerance of the species’ seeds to Al 3+ . Diaspores (seeds enclosed by the endocarp) were exposed to Al³⁺ (0, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 and 8000 µM L − 1 ) for 60 days. The histolocalization of Al³⁺ in the seed was performed, and viability, cell membrane functionality, and embryonic respiratory activity were evaluated. Al³⁺ retention by diaspore components was evaluated using quantitative and histochemical methods. Isolated embryos were immersed in the same solutions, and the quantification and histolocalization of Al³⁺ were performed, evaluating its effect on cell structure. Embryo viability and in vitro development were evaluated. The pericarpal structures and the seed coat restrict the penetration of Al³⁺ towards the endosperm and embryo, which maintains the physiological status of the seeds. In embryos, Al³⁺ is retained in the cell walls and also compartmentalized in vacuoles at the periphery of the cotyledon, thus preserving the embryo axis. In vitro development is not affected, and only 8000 µM L − 1 of Al³⁺ reduces embryo viability. Macaúba diaspores are highly tolerant to Al³⁺, exhibiting exclusion mechanisms in both pericarpal structures and embryonic cells. These mechanisms preserve the embryo axis and favor the species’ adaptation to vast regions of the Cerrado biome.

title: Selection and Application of an Aptamer for the Extraction and HPLC-MS/MS Determination of Six Perfluorinated Compounds in Food
abstractText: Abstract Recognition elements capable of recognizing multiple PFAS are needed for monitoring PFAS in food. Using Capture-SELEX with PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, and PFHxS as the selection targets, we isolated aptamer S1, which recognized these four compounds as well as PFHpA and PFHpS. Molecular docking and circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the shared and differential binding sites of S1 with these six PFAS, elucidating the structural basis for their recognition. S1 was immobilized onto streptavidin-coated magnetic beads to construct an Apt-MBs enrichment platform coupled with HPLC-MS/MS. The method exhibited linearity from 0.067 to 50 ng/mL (R2 > 0.997), low detection limits of 0.020–0.050 ng/mL, recoveries of 71.9%–99.3% in spiked meat samples, and relative standard deviations below 6%. This enrichment-LC-MS/MS dual-mode strategy provides a selective, sensitive, and stable tool for monitoring multicomponent PFAS in complex food matrices, with promising applications in nutritional safety assessment and dietary exposure monitoring.

title: Root length changes in the maxillary posterior segment following miniplate-anchored intrusion: A retrospective cone-beam computed tomography study
abstractText: Objectives: The objective of the study is to evaluate morphological changes and orthodontically induced root resorption (OIRR) across the maxillary posterior segment following miniplate-anchored intrusion using cone- beam computed tomography (CBCT). Material and Methods: This retrospective observational cohort study included 19 patients treated for anterior open bite with miniplate-supported intrusion of the maxillary posterior teeth. Pre-treatment (T0) and post- treatment (T1) CBCT scans were analyzed using in vivo software. Root length measurements of maxillary premolars, first molars, and second molars were measured from the central fossa to the root apex. Interrater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients > 0.76. Changes in root length between T0 and T1 were analyzed using paired t -tests (α = 0.05). Results: The greatest resorption was observed in the palatal root of the upper right first premolar (0.99 ± 0.41 mm; p = 0.025). Significant shortening was identified in palatal roots of the upper left second premolar (0.76 ± 0.18 mm; p < 0.001) and upper right second premolar (0.51 ± 0.20 mm; p = 0.0167). In first molars, the palatal and distobuccal roots showed the greatest resorption, reaching 0.98 ± 0.26 mm and 0.96 ± 0.21 mm, respectively ( p ≤ 0.001). Second molars demonstrated small, non-significant increases in root length (0.02–0.49 mm; p > 0.05), consistent with continued root development. Conclusion: Miniplate-anchored intrusion results in limited (<1 mm) and clinically acceptable root resorption in maxillary premolars and first molars, while second molars, likely reflecting a subset with incompletely formed apices, appeared resistant to OIRR.

title: Assessment of the Reproducibility of Experimental Results in Aqueous Alkaline Media Using Pt Electrodes
abstractText: Abstract Research in interfacial electrochemistry and electrocatalysis requires establishing standard experimental procedures and conditions that ensure reproducibility and reliability of results. While standard procedures for experimental research employing Pt electrodes in aqueous acidic solutions were established ca. 50 years ago, similar benchmarks for aqueous alkaline media do not exist. In this contribution, cyclic voltammetry (CV) experiments are performed in the 0.05–1.40 V range using polycrystalline and monocrystalline platinum electrodes (Pt(poly) and Pt(POSSC)) in 0.50 M aqueous H2SO4 (a reference electrolyte solution) and 0.10 M aqueous NaOH (a studied electrolyte solution) to verify the systems’ cleanliness and to determine the electrodes’ electrochemically active surface area (Aecsa). Afterward, chronoamperometry (CA) measurements are conducted by holding the applied potential at 0.50 V for various holding times in the 30–1,800 s range, and then Aecsa is re-evaluated by CV experiments. The results demonstrate that unavoidable contamination, present even in the highest purity chemicals and water, adsorbs on the surface of the Pt electrodes and reduces their Aecsa. The reduction in Aecsa increases with increasing the holding time in CA measurements. Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDS) spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses of the Pt(poly) and Pt(POSSC) electrodes reveal the presence of C and O-containing compounds in the case of aqueous H2SO4 solution and C, O, and Pb compounds in the case of aqueous NaOH solution. The results demonstrate the complementarity of electrochemical and surface science methods in assessing the cleanliness of electrode materials and highlight the need for rigorous experimental protocols that ensure reproducibility and reliability of experimental results.
